bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑第293卷

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 293
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 293

sentences.zh: 【後周紀四】起柔兆執徐三月，盡強圉大荒落，凡一年有奇。

translations.literal: [Later Zhou Records 4] From the third month of Rouzhao Zhixu through Qiangyu Dahuangluo, altogether slightly more than one year.
translations.idiomatic: [Later Zhou Records 4] From the third month of 956 through the end of 957—a period of slightly more than one year.

sentences.zh: 三月，甲午朔，上行視水寨，至淝橋，自取一石，馬上持之至寨以供砲，從官過橋者人繼一石。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the jiawu new moon, the Emperor went to inspect the water camp. At the Fei Bridge he took a stone himself, carried it on horseback to the camp to supply the catapults, and each attendant who crossed the bridge followed with a stone.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the first day of the month, the Emperor went to inspect the water camp. At the Fei Bridge he picked up a stone himself and, still mounted, carried it to the camp for the catapults; every official who crossed the bridge brought one stone after another.

sentences.zh: 太祖皇帝乘皮船入壽春壕中，城上發連弩射之，矢大如屋椽。

translations.literal: The Emperor boarded a leather boat and entered the moat at Shouchun. From atop the wall they loosed repeating crossbows at him; the bolts were as large as rafters.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor took a leather boat into the moat around Shouchun. Defenders on the walls fired repeating crossbows at him; the bolts were thick as roof beams.

sentences.zh: 牙將館陶張瓊遽以身蔽之，矢中瓊髀，死而復甦。

translations.literal: The junior general Zhang Qiong of Guantao hastily shielded him with his body. A bolt struck Qiong in the thigh; he died and came back to life.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qiong, a junior general from Guantao, threw himself in front of the Emperor. A bolt struck Qiong in the thigh; he briefly lost consciousness, then revived.

sentences.zh: 鏃著骨不可出，瓊飲酒一大卮，令人破骨出之。

translations.literal: The arrowhead lodged in the bone and could not be drawn out. Qiong drank a large cup of wine and had someone break the bone to remove it.
translations.idiomatic: The arrowhead had lodged in the bone and would not come out. Qiong downed a full cup of wine and had his attendants break the bone to extract it.

sentences.zh: 流血數升，神色自若。

translations.literal: He lost several sheng of blood, yet his expression remained calm.
translations.idiomatic: He lost several pints of blood, yet his bearing remained perfectly composed.

sentences.zh: 唐主復以右僕射孫晟為司空，遣與禮部尚書王崇質奉表入見，稱：「自天祐以來，海內分崩，或跨據一方，或遷革異代，臣紹襲先業，奄有江表，顧以瞻烏未定，附鳳何從！

translations.literal: The Tang ruler again appointed Right Vice Director Sun Sheng as Minister of Works and sent him with Minister of Rites Wang Chongzhi to present a memorial and have audience. It stated: "Since the Tianyou era, the realm has split apart—some holding one region, others passing through successive dynasties. Your servant has inherited his forebears' enterprise and suddenly holds the lands south of the Yangtze, yet with the crows still unsettled where shall one look, and to which phoenix may one attach!
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Tang ruler again named Sun Sheng, his Right Vice Director, Minister of Works, and sent him with Wang Chongzhi, Minister of Rites, to present a memorial at court. It read: "Since the Tianyou era the empire has shattered—lords have seized their own corners of the land or bowed to one new dynasty after another. I inherited my forefathers' realm and now hold the lower Yangtze, yet with the capital still undecided, where should I turn my gaze, and to which sovereign may I pledge myself?

sentences.zh: 今天命有歸，聲教遠被，願比兩浙、湖南，仰奉正朔，謹守土疆，乞收薄伐之威，赦其後服之罪，首於下國，俾作外臣，則柔遠之德，雲誰不服！」

translations.literal: Now that Heaven's mandate has found its place and your transforming influence reaches far, I wish to be like the Two Zhes and Hunan, to look up and accept your calendar, strictly to guard my territory, and to beg that you withdraw the might of a light punitive expedition and pardon the offense of tardy submission, that I as head of a lesser state may be made an outer vassal—then in your virtue of cherishing the distant, who would not submit!"
translations.idiomatic: Now that Heaven's mandate is settled and your civilizing rule reaches far, I ask to stand as the Two Zhes and Hunan do—to accept your calendar, hold my borders in peace, and beg you to stay the edge of your punitive campaign and forgive my delay in submitting. Let me, as ruler of a lesser state, serve as your outer vassal; with such kindness to the distant, who would not bow?"

sentences.zh: 又獻金千兩，銀十萬兩，羅綺二千匹。

translations.literal: He also presented one thousand taels of gold, one hundred thousand taels of silver, and two thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He also offered one thousand taels of gold, one hundred thousand taels of silver, and two thousand bolts of silk brocade.

sentences.zh: 晟謂馮延己曰：「此行當在左相，晟若辭之，則負先帝。」

translations.literal: Sheng said to Feng Yanji: "This mission ought to fall to the Left Chancellor. If Sheng declines it, he will fail the late emperor."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng told Feng Yanji, "This embassy should have been the Left Chancellor's task. If I refused it, I would betray our late emperor."

sentences.zh: 既行，知不免，中夜，歎息謂崇質曰：「君家百口，宜自為謀。

translations.literal: Once he had set out, knowing he could not escape, in the middle of the night he sighed and said to Chongzhi: "Your household has a hundred mouths; you should look to your own safety.
translations.idiomatic: After they departed, knowing he would not return, he sighed in the dead of night and told Chongzhi, "Your family numbers a hundred souls—you must plan for yourselves.

sentences.zh: 吾思之熟矣，終不負永陵一培土，餘無所知。」

translations.literal: I have thought it through thoroughly: I will never fail the one mound of earth at Yongling; beyond that I know nothing."
translations.idiomatic: I have weighed it carefully: I will never betray the one mound of earth at Yongling—the tomb of our founder—and beyond that I know nothing."

sentences.zh: 南漢甘泉宮使林延遇，陰險多計數，南漢主倚信之；

translations.literal: Lin Yanyu, commissioner of the Sweet Springs Palace of Southern Han, was sinister and full of stratagems; the Southern Han ruler relied on and trusted him;
translations.idiomatic: Lin Yanyu, commissioner of the Sweet Springs Palace in Southern Han, was treacherous and endlessly scheming, and the Southern Han ruler placed great trust in him;

sentences.zh: 誅滅諸弟，皆延遇之謀也。

translations.literal: the execution and extermination of all his younger brothers were Yanyu's plots.
translations.idiomatic: the slaughter of the ruler's younger brothers had all been Yanyu's doing.

sentences.zh: 乙未卒，國人相賀。

translations.literal: On the yiyi day he died, and the people of the state congratulated one another.
translations.idiomatic: On the yiyi day he died, and people across the realm celebrated.

sentences.zh: 延遇病甚，薦內給事龔澄樞自代，南漢主即日擢澄樞知承宣院及內侍省。

translations.literal: When Yanyu fell gravely ill, he recommended the inner attendant Gong Chengsu to succeed him, and that same day the Southern Han ruler promoted Chengsu to oversee the Court of Imperial Communications and the Palace Domestic Service.
translations.idiomatic: As Yanyu lay dying, he recommended the inner attendant Gong Chengsu as his successor, and the Southern Han ruler that same day put Chengsu in charge of the Court of Imperial Communications and the Palace Domestic Service.

sentences.zh: 澄樞，番禺人也。

translations.literal: Chengsu was a man of Panyu.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsu was a native of Panyu.

sentences.zh: 光、舒、黃招安巡檢使、行光州刺史何超以安、隨、申、蔡四州兵數萬攻光州。

translations.literal: He Chao, Pacification and Inspection Commissioner for Guang, Shu, and Huang and acting prefect of Guangzhou, led several tens of thousands of troops from An, Sui, Shen, and Cai to attack Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He Chao, commissioner charged with pacifying Guang, Shu, and Huang and acting prefect of Guangzhou, marched tens of thousands of men from An, Sui, Shen, and Cai against Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 丙申，超奏唐光州刺史張紹棄城走，都監張承翰以城降。

translations.literal: On the bingshen day, Chao reported that Tang Prefect of Guangzhou Zhang Shao had abandoned the city and fled, and the garrison commander Zhang Chenghan had surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingshen day, He Chao reported that the Tang prefect Zhang Shao had fled Guangzhou and that the garrison commander Zhang Chenghan had surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，行舒州刺史郭令圖拔舒州。

translations.literal: On the dingyou day, Guo Lingtu, acting prefect of Shuzhou, captured Shuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingyou day, Guo Lingtu, acting prefect of Shuzhou, took the city.

sentences.zh: 唐蘄州將李福殺其知州王承巂，舉州來降。

translations.literal: The Tang general Li Fu of Qizhou killed its prefect Wang Chengyu and brought the whole prefecture to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fu, a Tang officer in Qizhou, killed the prefect Wang Chengyu and surrendered the entire prefecture.

sentences.zh: 遣六宅使齊藏珍攻黃州。

translations.literal: The Emperor dispatched the Six Residences envoy Qi Cangzhen to attack Huangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Qi Cangzhen, an envoy of the Six Residences, to attack Huangzhou.

sentences.zh: 彰武留後李彥頵，性貪虐，部民與羌胡作亂，攻之。

translations.literal: Li Yanwen, acting commissioner of Zhangwu, was by nature greedy and cruel; the people of his commandery rose in revolt with Qiang and Hu and attacked him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yanwen, acting commissioner of Zhangwu, was greedy and brutal; tribesmen and local people rebelled and attacked him.

sentences.zh: 上召彥頵還朝。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned Yanwen back to court.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor recalled Yanwen to the capital.

sentences.zh: 秦、鳳之平也，上赦所俘蜀兵以隸軍籍，從征淮南，覆亡降於唐。

translations.literal: When Qin and Feng were pacified, the Emperor pardoned captured Shu soldiers and enrolled them in the army rolls; on the Huainan campaign they were wiped out and surrendered to Tang.
translations.idiomatic: After the pacification of Qin and Feng, the Emperor had pardoned captured Shu troops and enrolled them in the army; on the Huainan campaign they were destroyed to the last man and defected to the Tang.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，唐主表獻百五十人；

translations.literal: On the guimao day, the Tang ruler memorialized offering one hundred fifty men;
translations.idiomatic: On the guimao day, the Tang ruler sent a memorial offering one hundred fifty men;

sentences.zh: 上悉命斬之。

translations.literal: the Emperor ordered all of them beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: the Emperor ordered every one of them executed.

sentences.zh: 舒州人逐郭令圖，鐵騎都指揮使洛陽王審琦選輕騎夜襲舒州，復取之，令圖乃得歸。

translations.literal: The people of Shuzhou drove out Guo Lingtu. Wang Shenqi of Luoyang, commander of the Iron Cavalry, selected light horsemen for a night assault on Shuzhou, retook it, and only then could Lingtu return.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Shuzhou expelled Guo Lingtu. Wang Shenqi of Luoyang, commander of the Iron Cavalry, led a night raid with picked light cavalry, recaptured the city, and only then could Lingtu come back.

sentences.zh: 馬希崇及王延政之子繼沂皆在揚州，詔撫存之。

translations.literal: Ma Xichong and Wang Yanzheng's son Jiyi were both at Yangzhou; an edict ordered that they be comforted and provided for.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xichong and Wang Yanzheng's son Jiyi were both at Yangzhou; the court issued an edict to treat them kindly and provide for them.

sentences.zh: 丙午，孫晟等至上所。

translations.literal: On the bingwu day, Sun Sheng and the others reached the Emperor's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingwu day, Sun Sheng and his party arrived at the imperial camp.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，上遣中使以孫晟詣壽春城下，示劉仁贍，且招諭之。

translations.literal: On the gengxu day, the Emperor sent a palace envoy to take Sun Sheng to beneath the walls of Shouchun, show him to Liu Renshan, and also summon and instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengxu day, the Emperor sent a palace envoy to bring Sun Sheng to the foot of Shouchun's walls, display him to Liu Renshan, and urge him to surrender.

sentences.zh: 仁贍見晟，戎服拜於城上。

translations.literal: When Renshan saw Sheng, he bowed in military dress atop the wall.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Renshan saw Sun Sheng, he bowed from atop the wall in full armor.

sentences.zh: 晟謂仁贍曰：「君受國厚恩，不可開門納寇。」

translations.literal: Sheng said to Renshan: "You have received thick grace from the state; you must not open the gates and admit invaders."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng told Liu Renshan, "You owe the state a great debt of gratitude—you must not open the gates to the enemy."

sentences.zh: 上聞之，甚怒，晟曰：「臣為唐宰相，豈可教節度使外叛邪！」

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard of it he was greatly angry. Sheng said: "Your servant is a Tang chancellor—how could he teach a military commissioner to defect to the outside!"
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor heard this he was furious. Sun Sheng said, "I am a Tang chancellor—how could I urge a military commissioner to betray his sovereign?"

sentences.zh: 上乃釋之。

translations.literal: The Emperor then released him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then let the matter go.

sentences.zh: 唐主使李德明、孫晟言於上，請去帝號，割壽、濠、泗、楚、光、海六州之地。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler sent Li Deming and Sun Sheng to speak to the Emperor, asking to relinquish the imperial title and cede the six prefectures of Shou, Hao, Si, Chu, Guang, and Hai.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang ruler sent Li Deming and Sun Sheng to propose abandoning the imperial title and yielding the six prefectures of Shou, Hao, Si, Chu, Guang, and Hai.

sentences.zh: 仍歲輸金帛百萬以求罷兵。

translations.literal: They would also pay one million in gold and silk each year to seek an end to hostilities.
translations.idiomatic: They would also pay one million strings' worth of gold and silk annually in exchange for peace.

sentences.zh: 上以淮南之地已半為周有，諸將捷奏日至，欲盡得江北之地，不許。

translations.literal: The Emperor, since half of Huainan was already Zhou territory and daily victory reports arrived from the generals, wished to take all the lands north of the Yangtze and did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Half of Huainan was already Zhou territory, and victory dispatches arrived daily; the Emperor meant to take all the land north of the Yangtze and refused.

sentences.zh: 德明見周兵日進，奏稱：「唐主不知陛下兵力如此之盛，願寬臣五日之誅，得歸白唐主，盡獻江北之地。」

translations.literal: Deming, seeing Zhou troops advancing day by day, memorialized: "The Tang ruler does not know how mighty Your Majesty's forces are. I beg a five-day reprieve from execution so I may return and inform the Tang ruler, and he will yield all the territory north of the Yangtze."
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Zhou forces advance daily, Li Deming pleaded, "Our ruler had no idea your armies were this strong. Grant me five days' grace from death so I may return, tell him, and he will surrender all the territory north of the Yangtze."

sentences.zh: 上乃許之。

translations.literal: The Emperor then granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 晟因奏遣王崇質與德明俱歸。

translations.literal: Sheng thereupon memorialized to send Wang Chongzhi back together with Deming.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng then asked that Wang Chongzhi be allowed to return with Li Deming.

sentences.zh: 上遣供奉官安弘道送德明等歸金陵，賜唐主詔，其略曰：「但存帝號，何爽歲寒！

translations.literal: The Emperor sent the tribute officer An Hongdao to escort Deming and the others back to Jinling and bestowed an edict on the Tang ruler, which in summary said: "If you but keep your imperial title, what harm in the cold of winter!
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent the tribute officer An Hongdao to escort Li Deming home to Jinling and issued an edict to the Tang ruler that read in part: "Keep your imperial title—what is a season's cold to a pine?

sentences.zh: 倘堅事大之心，終不迫人於險。」

translations.literal: If you steadfastly keep the heart of serving the greater power, in the end I will not drive men into peril."
translations.idiomatic: If you hold firm to your duty as the lesser power, I will never drive you to desperation."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「俟諸郡之悉來，即大軍之立罷。

translations.literal: It also said: "When all the commanderies have come in, the great army will at once withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: It also said, "Once every prefecture has submitted, the main army will withdraw at once.

sentences.zh: 言盡於此，更不煩雲，苟曰未然，請從茲絕。」

translations.literal: My words end here; I will trouble you no further. If you say it is not so, let us break off from this point."
translations.idiomatic: That is all I have to say, and I will not trouble you further. If you disagree, let us end the matter here."

sentences.zh: 又賜其將相書，使熟議而來。

translations.literal: He also sent letters to Tang generals and ministers, telling them to deliberate thoroughly and then come.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote to the Tang generals and ministers, telling them to deliberate carefully and then reply.

sentences.zh: 唐主復上表謝。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler again submitted a memorial of thanks.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang ruler sent another memorial of thanks.

sentences.zh: 李德明盛稱上威德及甲兵之強，勸唐主豁江北之地，唐主不悅。

translations.literal: Li Deming lavishly praised the Emperor's majesty and virtue and the strength of his armor and troops, urging the Tang ruler to give up the lands north of the Yangtze; the Tang ruler was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deming spoke at length of the Zhou Emperor's might and the power of his armies, urging the Tang ruler to surrender all territory north of the Yangtze; the Tang ruler was displeased.

sentences.zh: 宋齊丘以割地為無益，德明輕佻，言多過實，國人亦不之信。

translations.literal: Song Qiqiu held that ceding territory was of no benefit; Deming was frivolous and his words often exceeded the facts, and the people of the state also did not believe him.
translations.idiomatic: Song Qiqiu argued that yielding territory would do no good; Li Deming was flighty and his reports exaggerated, and the court did not trust him either.

sentences.zh: 樞密使陳覺、副使李徵古素惡德明與孫晟，使王崇質異其言，因譖德明於唐主曰：「德明賣國求利。」

translations.literal: Chen Jue, Commissioner of Military Affairs, and Vice Commissioner Li Zhenggu had long hated Deming and Sun Sheng; they had Wang Chongzhi contradict his account and slandered Deming to the Tang ruler, saying: "Deming sold the state for profit."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jue, Commissioner of Military Affairs, and his deputy Li Zhenggu had long hated Li Deming and Sun Sheng; they had Wang Chongzhi contradict Deming's report and told the Tang ruler, "Li Deming sold out the realm for his own gain."

sentences.zh: 唐主大怒，斬德明於市。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler was greatly enraged and executed Deming in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang ruler was furious and had Li Deming executed in public.

sentences.zh: 吳程攻常州，破其外郭，執唐常州團練使趙仁澤，送於錢唐，仁澤見吳越王弘俶不拜，責以負約。

translations.literal: Wu Cheng attacked Changzhou, broke its outer wall, seized the Tang defense commissioner of Changzhou Zhao Renze, and sent him to Qiantang. When Renze saw the King of Wuyue Hong Chu he did not bow and rebuked him for breaking his pledge.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Cheng attacked Changzhou, breached its outer defenses, captured the Tang defense commissioner Zhao Renze, and sent him to Qiantang. Zhao Renze refused to bow to King Hong Chu of Wuyue and accused him of breaking his word.

sentences.zh: 弘俶怒，抉其口至耳。

translations.literal: Hong Chu was enraged and gouged his mouth as far as the ear.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Chu flew into a rage and ripped his mouth open to the ear.

sentences.zh: 元德昭憐其忠，為傅良藥，得不死。

translations.literal: Yuan Dezhao pitied his loyalty, applied good medicine for him, and he did not die.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Dezhao admired his loyalty, treated him with good medicine, and he survived.

sentences.zh: 唐主以吳越兵在常州，恐其侵逼潤州，以宣、潤大都督燕王弘冀年少，恐其不習兵，徵還金陵。

translations.literal: Because Wuyue troops were at Changzhou, the Tang ruler feared they would press upon Runzhou; as the Prince of Yan Hong Ji, Grand Commander of Xuan and Run, was young and he feared he was not versed in warfare, he summoned him back to Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: With Wuyue forces at Changzhou, the Tang ruler feared an attack on Runzhou; he also worried that Prince Hong Ji of Yan, grand commander of Xuan and Run, was too young and inexperienced, and recalled him to Jinling.

sentences.zh: 部將趙鐸言於弘冀曰：「大王元帥，眾心所恃，逆自退歸，所部必亂。」

translations.literal: The staff officer Zhao Duo said to Hong Ji: "Your Highness is commander-in-chief and the hearts of the masses rely on you. If you withdraw on your own initiative, your command will surely fall into disorder."
translations.idiomatic: His officer Zhao Duo told Hong Ji, "You are the commander the men trust. If you withdraw on your own, the army will collapse."

sentences.zh: 弘冀然之，辭不就徵，部分諸將，為戰守之備。

translations.literal: Hong Ji agreed, declined the summons, deployed the generals, and made preparations for attack and defense.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Ji agreed, refused the recall, deployed his generals, and prepared for both attack and defense.

sentences.zh: 龍武都虞候柴克宏，再用之子也，沉默好施，不事家產，雖典宿衛，日與賓客博奕飲酒，未嘗言兵，時人以為非將帥才。

translations.literal: Chai Kehong, deputy commander of the Dragon Martial Guard, was a son of Chai Zaiyong. He was taciturn and fond of giving; he did not attend to family property. Though he held charge of the palace guard, day after day he gambled and drank with guests and never spoke of military matters; people of the time thought him no material for a general.
translations.idiomatic: Chai Kehong, deputy commander of the Dragon Martial Guard, was a son of Chai Zaiyong. Taciturn and generous, he ignored his estates; though he held a palace guard post, he spent his days gambling and drinking with guests and never spoke of war, and contemporaries judged him no general.

sentences.zh: 至是，有言克宏久不遷官者，唐主以為撫州刺史。

translations.literal: At this time someone said Kehong had long gone without promotion; the Tang ruler appointed him prefect of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Now someone remarked that Kehong had long gone without promotion, and the Tang ruler named him prefect of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 克宏請效死行陳，其母亦表稱克宏有父風，可為將，苟不勝任，分甘孥戮。

translations.literal: Kehong requested to offer his life in the ranks. His mother also submitted a memorial saying Kehong had his father's bearing and could serve as a general; if he should prove unfit, she would gladly share punishment with her kin.
translations.idiomatic: Kehong asked to die in the front lines if need be. His mother memorialized that he had his father's martial spirit and could command troops; if he failed, their whole family would accept punishment.

sentences.zh: 唐主乃以克宏為右武衛將軍，使將兵會袁州刺史陸孟俊救常州。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler then made Kehong General of the Right Martial Guard and sent him to lead troops to join Yuanzhou Prefect Lu Mengjun in relieving Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang ruler then made Kehong a general of the Right Martial Guard and ordered him to join Lu Mengjun, prefect of Yuanzhou, in relieving Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 時唐精兵悉在江北，克宏所將數千人皆羸老，樞密使李徵古復以鎧仗之朽蠹者給之。

translations.literal: At that time all Tang crack troops were north of the Yangtze; the several thousand men Kehong led were all weak and old, and Commissioner Li Zhenggu again supplied them with armor and weapons that were rotten and worm-eaten.
translations.idiomatic: All Tang elite troops were already north of the Yangtze; the few thousand men under Kehong were weak and elderly, and Li Zhenggu deliberately issued them rotting armor and worm-eaten weapons.

sentences.zh: 克宏訴於徵古，徵古慢罵之，眾皆憤恚，克宏怡然。

translations.literal: Kehong complained to Zhenggu; Zhenggu insulted and reviled him. The troops were all furious, but Kehong remained at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Kehong protested to Li Zhenggu, who answered with contempt and abuse. The men seethed with anger, but Kehong remained calm.

sentences.zh: 至潤州，徵古遣使召還，以神衛統軍朱匡業代之。

translations.literal: When he reached Runzhou, Zhenggu sent a messenger to recall him and replaced him with Zhu Kuangye, commander of the Divine Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At Runzhou, Li Zhenggu sent orders to recall him and replace him with Zhu Kuangye, commander of the Divine Guard.

sentences.zh: 燕王弘冀謂克宏：「君但前戰，吾當論奏。」

translations.literal: Prince Hong Ji said to Kehong: "You need only press forward in battle; I will memorialize on your behalf."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Hong Ji told Kehong, "Fight on—I will plead your case at court."

sentences.zh: 乃表克宏才略可以成功，常州危在旦莫，不宜中易主將。

translations.literal: He then memorialized that Kehong's talent and strategy could succeed, that Changzhou's peril was imminent, and that it was unsuitable to change commanders midway.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that Kehong had the talent to win, that Changzhou could fall at any moment, and that swapping commanders mid-campaign would be disastrous.

sentences.zh: 克宏引兵徑趣常州，徵古復遣使召之，克宏曰：「吾計日破賊，汝來召吾，必奸人也！」

translations.literal: Kehong led his troops straight for Changzhou. Zhenggu again sent a messenger to summon him. Kehong said: "I count the days until I break the enemy. You come to summon me—you must be a traitor!"
translations.idiomatic: Kehong marched straight for Changzhou. Li Zhenggu sent another recall. Kehong said, "I will crush the enemy within days. Anyone who summons me now is a traitor!"

sentences.zh: 命斬之。

translations.literal: He ordered him beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: He had the messenger executed.

sentences.zh: 使者曰：「受李樞密命而來。」

translations.literal: The messenger said: "I come on Commissioner Li's order."
translations.idiomatic: The messenger cried, "I come on Commissioner Li's orders!"

sentences.zh: 克宏曰：「李樞密來，吾亦斬之！」

translations.literal: Kehong said: "If Commissioner Li comes, I will behead him too!"
translations.idiomatic: Kehong replied, "If Li Zhenggu comes himself, I will behead him too!"

sentences.zh: 初，鮑修讓、羅晟在福州，與吳程有隙，至是，程抑挫之，二人皆怨。

translations.literal: Earlier, Bao Xiurang and Luo Sheng had been at Fuzhou and had a rift with Wu Cheng; now Cheng suppressed and humiliated them, and both bore resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Bao Xiurang and Luo Sheng had served at Fuzhou and clashed with Wu Cheng; now Cheng humiliated them, and both nursed a grudge.

sentences.zh: 先是，唐主遣中書舍人喬匡舜使於吳越，壬子，柴克宏至常州，蒙其船以幕，匿甲士於其中，聲言迎匡舜。

translations.literal: Earlier the Tang ruler had sent Zhongshu Sheren Qiao Kuangshun as envoy to Wuyue. On the renzi day, Chai Kehong reached Changzhou, covered his boats with curtains, hid armored men within, and proclaimed that he was coming to welcome Kuangshun.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang ruler had earlier sent Qiao Kuangshun, a Secretariat drafter, as envoy to Wuyue. On the renzi day Chai Kehong reached Changzhou, draped his boats in canvas, hid armored men aboard, and announced that he had come to welcome Qiao Kuangshun.

sentences.zh: 吳越邏者以告，程曰：「兵交，使在其間，不可妄以為疑。」

translations.literal: Wuyue scouts reported it. Cheng said: "Armies are engaged and an envoy is between them; one must not rashly treat this as suspicious."
translations.idiomatic: Wuyue scouts reported the approach. Wu Cheng said, "Armies are at war and an envoy is between us—we must not suspect treachery lightly."

sentences.zh: 唐兵登岸，逕薄吳越營，羅晟不力戰，縱之使趣程帳，程僅以身免。

translations.literal: Tang troops went ashore and pressed straight on the Wuyue camp. Luo Sheng did not fight hard but let them drive toward Cheng's headquarters; Cheng barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: Tang troops landed and charged straight at the Wuyue camp. Luo Sheng held back and let them rush Wu Cheng's headquarters; Cheng barely escaped alive.

sentences.zh: 克宏大破吳越兵，斬首萬級。

translations.literal: Kehong inflicted a great defeat on Wuyue troops and took ten thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Kehong routed the Wuyue army and claimed ten thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 朱匡業至行營，克宏事之甚謹。

translations.literal: When Zhu Kuangye reached the field headquarters, Kehong served him with great deference.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Kuangye arrived at camp, Kehong treated him with scrupulous respect.

sentences.zh: 吳程至錢唐，吳越王弘俶悉奪其官。

translations.literal: When Wu Cheng reached Qiantang, the King of Wuyue Hong Chu stripped him of all his offices.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Cheng reached Qiantang, King Hong Chu of Wuyue stripped him of every office.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，蜀主以捧聖控鶴都指揮使李廷珪為左右衛聖諸軍馬步都指揮使，仍分衛聖、匡聖步騎為左右十軍，以武定節度使呂彥琦等為使，廷珪總之，如趙廷隱之任。

translations.literal: On the jiayin day, the Shu ruler appointed Li Tinggui, commander of the Paladin Crane Guard, Grand Commander of the Left and Right Imperial Guard Armies of infantry and cavalry; he also divided the Imperial Guard and Support-the-Sage infantry and cavalry into left and right ten armies, with Military Commissioners such as Lü Yanqi of Wuding as commanders, with Tinggui overseeing all, like Zhao Tingyin's post.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiayin day the Shu ruler named Li Tinggui, commander of the Paladin Crane Guard, supreme commander of the left and right imperial guard forces; he split the guard and Support-the-Sage infantry and cavalry into ten armies on each flank, with commissioners such as Lü Yanqi of Wuding in command while Tinggui held overall authority, as Zhao Tingyin had once done.

sentences.zh: 初，柴克宏為宣州巡檢使，始至，城塹不修，器械皆闕，吏云：「自田頵、王茂章、李遇相繼叛，後人無敢治之者。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when Chai Kehong was inspection commissioner of Xuanzhou, on first arrival the walls and moats were unrepaired and weapons were all lacking. The clerks said: "Since Tian Jun, Wang Maozhang, and Li Yu rebelled in succession, no successor has dared to repair them."
translations.idiomatic: When Chai Kehong first became inspection commissioner of Xuanzhou, the walls and moats were in ruins and the armory empty. His staff said, "Ever since Tian Jun, Wang Maozhang, and Li Yu rebelled one after another, no one has dared repair them."

sentences.zh: 克宏曰：「時移事異，安有此理！」

translations.literal: Kehong said: "Times have changed and affairs are different—how can there be such a principle!"
translations.idiomatic: Kehong said, "Times have changed—how can we accept that excuse!"

sentences.zh: 悉繕完之。

translations.literal: He had everything repaired and made complete.
translations.idiomatic: He had everything restored.

sentences.zh: 由是路彥銖攻之不克，聞吳程敗，乙卯，引歸。

translations.literal: Because of this Lu Yanzhen attacked but could not take it. Hearing of Wu Cheng's defeat, on the yimao day he withdrew and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yanzhen besieged it without success; when he heard of Wu Cheng's defeat, he withdrew on the yimao day.

sentences.zh: 唐主以克宏為奉化節度使，克宏復請將兵救壽州，未至而卒。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler made Kehong Military Commissioner of Fenghua. Kehong again asked to lead troops to relieve Shouchun but died before he arrived.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang ruler made Kehong military commissioner of Fenghua. Kehong again asked to march to relieve Shouchun but died before he could set out.

sentences.zh: 河陽節度使白重贊以天子南征，慮北漢乘虛入寇，繕完守備，且請兵於西京。

translations.literal: Bai Chongzan, Military Commissioner of Heyang, because the Son of Heaven was campaigning south, feared that Northern Han would seize the opportunity to invade; he repaired defenses and also requested troops from the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Chongzan, military commissioner of Heyang, feared that Northern Han would strike while the Emperor campaigned south; he strengthened his defenses and asked the Western Capital for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 西京留守王晏初不之與，又慮事出非常，乃自將兵赴之。

translations.literal: Wang Yan, defender of the Western Capital, at first did not give them; then fearing something extraordinary might occur, he led troops there himself.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan, defender of the Western Capital, at first refused; then, fearing an emergency, he marched there in person.

sentences.zh: 重贊以晏不奉詔而來，拒不納，遣人謂之曰：「令公昔在陝服，已立大功，河陽小城，不煩枉駕！」

translations.literal: Chongzan, because Yan had come without imperial order, refused to admit him and sent someone to say: "Your Lordship once served in the Shaan region and already achieved great merit; this little city of Heyang does not require your honored presence!"
translations.idiomatic: Chongzan, angry that Yan had come without orders, refused him entry and sent word: "You won great glory in Shaanxi long ago—a small post like Heyang hardly needs you in person!"

sentences.zh: 晏慚怍而還。

translations.literal: Yan withdrew in shame.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan withdrew in humiliation.

sentences.zh: 孟、洛之民，數日驚擾。

translations.literal: The people of Meng and Luo were alarmed and disturbed for several days.
translations.idiomatic: For days the people of Mengzhou and Luoyang were thrown into panic.

sentences.zh: 唐主命諸道兵馬元帥齊王景達將兵拒周，以陳覺為監軍使，前武安節度使邊鎬為應援都軍使。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler ordered the Commander-in-Chief of All Circuits' Armies and Horses, Prince Jingda of Qi, to lead troops to resist Zhou, with Chen Jue as army supervisor and the former Military Commissioner of Wu'an Bian Hao as overall relief commander.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang ruler ordered Prince Jingda of Qi, commander-in-chief of all circuits, to resist the Zhou, with Chen Jue as army supervisor and the former Wu'an commissioner Bian Hao as overall relief commander.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人韓熙載上書曰：「信莫信於親王，重莫重於元帥，安用監軍使為！」

translations.literal: Zhongshu Sheren Han Xizai submitted a memorial saying: "Whom should one trust if not an imperial prince? What is heavier than a commander-in-chief? What need is there for an army supervisor!"
translations.idiomatic: Han Xizai, a Secretariat drafter, memorialized: "Whom can you trust more than a prince of the blood? What office outweighs the commander-in-chief? Why send an army supervisor at all?"

sentences.zh: 唐主不從。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler did not follow it.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang ruler ignored him.

sentences.zh: 遣鴻臚卿潘承祐詣泉、建召募驍勇，承祐薦前永安節度使許文稹、靜江指揮使陳德誠、建州人鄭彥華、林仁肇。

translations.literal: He sent Grand Master of Ceremonies Pan Chengyou to Quan and Jian to recruit fierce warriors. Chengyou recommended the former Military Commissioner of Yong'an Xu Wenzhen, commander of Jingjiang Chen Decheng, and the Jianzhou men Zheng Yanhua and Lin Renzhao.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Pan Chengyou, Grand Master of Ceremonies, to Quanzhou and Jianzhou to recruit fierce fighters. Chengyou recommended the former Yong'an commissioner Xu Wenzhen, the Jingjiang commander Chen Decheng, and two men from Jianzhou, Zheng Yanhua and Lin Renzhao.

sentences.zh: 唐主以文稹為西面行營應援使，彥華、仁肇皆為將。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler made Wenzhen relief commissioner of the western field headquarters and made both Yanhua and Renzhao generals.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang ruler named Xu Wenzhen relief commissioner of the western field army and made Zheng Yanhua and Lin Renzhao generals.

sentences.zh: 仁肇，仁翰之弟也。

translations.literal: Renzhao was the younger brother of Renhan.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Renzhao was the younger brother of Lin Renhan.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，甲子，以侍衛新軍都指揮使、歸德節度使李重進為廬、壽等州招討使，以武寧節度使武行德為濠州城下都部署。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the jiazi day, Li Chongjin, commander of the New Palace Guard and Military Commissioner of Guide, was made Pacification Commissioner for Lu, Shou, and other prefectures, and Wu Xingde, Military Commissioner of Wuning, was made overall deployer beneath the walls of Haozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the jiazi day, Li Chongjin, commander of the New Palace Guard and commissioner of Guide, was named pacification commissioner for Lu, Shou, and neighboring prefectures, and Wu Xingde, commissioner of Wuning, was placed in overall command beneath the walls of Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 唐右衛將軍陸孟俊自常州將兵萬餘人趣泰州，周兵遁去，孟俊復取之，遣陳德誠戍泰州。

translations.literal: Lu Mengjun, General of the Tang Right Guard, led more than ten thousand men from Changzhou toward Taizhou. Zhou troops fled; Mengjun retook it and sent Chen Decheng to garrison Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Mengjun, a Tang general of the Right Guard, marched more than ten thousand men from Changzhou toward Taizhou. The Zhou forces withdrew; Mengjun recovered the city and left Chen Decheng to garrison it.

sentences.zh: 孟俊進攻揚州，屯於蜀岡，韓令坤棄揚州走。

translations.literal: Mengjun advanced to attack Yangzhou and encamped on Shugang. Han Lingkun abandoned Yangzhou and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Mengjun pressed on against Yangzhou and camped on Shugang. Han Lingkun abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 帝遣張永德將兵救之，令坤復入揚州。

translations.literal: The Emperor dispatched Zhang Yongde to lead troops to relieve them, and Lingkun re-entered Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor dispatched Zhang Yongde with troops to relieve them, and Han Lingkun reoccupied Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝又遣太祖皇帝將兵屯六合。

translations.literal: The Emperor also sent the Taizu Emperor to lead troops and encamp at Liuhe.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor also sent Zhao Kuangyin to lead troops and encamp at Liuhe.

sentences.zh: 太祖皇帝令曰：「揚州兵有過六合者，折其足！」

translations.literal: The Taizu Emperor issued an order, saying: "Any Yangzhou soldier who passes Liuhe shall have his legs broken!
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Kuangyin issued an order: "Any soldier from Yangzhou who passes Liuhe shall have his legs broken!"

sentences.zh: 令坤始有固守之志。

translations.literal: Only then did Lingkun first resolve to hold firm and defend.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did Han Lingkun resolve at last to stand firm and defend the city.

sentences.zh: 帝自至壽春以來，命諸軍晝夜攻城，久不克。

translations.literal: Since the Emperor had personally arrived at Shouchun, he ordered the various armies to assault the city day and night, yet for a long time they could not capture it.
translations.idiomatic: From the time the Emperor arrived in person at Shouchun, he ordered the armies to assault the walls day and night, but the city long remained uncaptured.

sentences.zh: 會大雨，營中水深數尺，攻具及士卒失亡頗多，糧運不繼，李德明失期不至，乃議旋師。

translations.literal: There happened to be a great rain; water in the camps stood several feet deep; siege engines and soldiers were lost in considerable numbers; grain transport could not keep up; Li Deming failed to arrive by the appointed time; and so they deliberated on withdrawing the army.
translations.idiomatic: Then heavy rains fell, and water stood several feet deep in the camps. Many siege engines and soldiers were lost, supply lines faltered, and Li Deming failed to appear when expected. The commanders began to discuss withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 或勸帝東幸濠州，聲言壽州已破，從之。

translations.literal: Someone advised the Emperor to travel east to Haozhou, proclaiming that Shouchun had already fallen, and he followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Some advisers urged the Emperor to travel east to Haozhou while spreading word that Shouchun had already fallen; he agreed.

sentences.zh: 己巳，帝自壽春循淮而東，乙亥，至濠州。

translations.literal: On the jisi day, the Emperor went from Shouchun eastward along the Huai; on the yihai day, he reached Haozhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, the Emperor departed Shouchun and followed the Huai River eastward; on yihai he arrived at Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 韓令坤敗唐兵於城東，擒陸孟俊。

translations.literal: Han Lingkun defeated Tang troops east of the city and captured Lu Mengjun.
translations.idiomatic: Han Lingkun routed the Southern Tang forces east of the city and took Lu Mengjun prisoner.

sentences.zh: 初，孟俊之廢馬希萼立希崇也，滅故舒州刺史楊昭惲之族而取其財。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Mengjun had deposed Ma Xiee and installed Ma Xichong, he exterminated the clan of the former Shuzhou prefect Yang Zhaoyun and seized their wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Mengjun had overthrown Ma Xiee and enthroned Ma Xichong, he had wiped out the entire house of Yang Zhaoyun, former prefect of Shuzhou, and seized their property.

sentences.zh: 楊氏有女美，獻於希崇。

translations.literal: The Yang family had a beautiful daughter, who was presented to Xichong.
translations.idiomatic: The Yangs had a daughter of striking beauty, whom they presented to Ma Xichong.

sentences.zh: 令坤入揚州，希崇以楊氏遺令坤，令坤嬖之。

translations.literal: When Lingkun entered Yangzhou, Xichong bestowed Lady Yang upon Lingkun, and Lingkun took her as a favored concubine.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Lingkun entered Yangzhou, Ma Xichong presented Lady Yang to him as a gift, and Lingkun took her as his favored concubine.

sentences.zh: 既獲孟俊，將械送帝所。

translations.literal: After capturing Mengjun, he was about to send him in chains to the Emperor's presence.
translations.idiomatic: Once Mengjun was captured, Lingkun prepared to send him under restraint to the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 楊氏在簾下，忽撫膺慟哭。

translations.literal: Lady Yang was behind the curtain; suddenly she clutched her breast and wept bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yang stood behind a screen and suddenly, clutching her breast, burst into violent weeping.

sentences.zh: 令坤驚問之，對曰：「孟俊昔在潭州，殺妾家二百口。

translations.literal: Lingkun, startled, asked her; she replied: "Mengjun, when he was at Tanzhou, killed two hundred members of my family.
translations.idiomatic: Startled, Lingkun asked what was wrong. She answered: "When Mengjun was in Tanzhou, he slaughtered two hundred souls of my household.

sentences.zh: 今見之，請復其冤。」

translations.literal: Now that I see him, I beg to avenge this wrong."
translations.idiomatic: Now that I see him before me, I ask that this wrong be avenged."

sentences.zh: 令坤乃殺之。

translations.literal: Lingkun then killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Lingkun then had him put to death.

sentences.zh: 唐齊王景達將兵二萬自瓜步濟江，距六合二十餘里，設柵不進。

translations.literal: The Tang Prince of Qi, Jing Da, led twenty thousand troops, crossed the river from Guabu, halted within a little over twenty li of Liuhe, set up palisades, and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Da, Prince of Qi of the Southern Tang, crossed the Yangtze from Guabu with twenty thousand men, halted some twenty-odd li from Liuhe, and dug in behind palisades without advancing further.

sentences.zh: 諸將欲擊之，太祖皇帝曰：「彼設柵自固，懼我也。

translations.literal: The various generals wished to attack them; the Taizu Emperor said: "They set up palisades to fortify themselves—they fear us.
translations.idiomatic: The generals wanted to strike at once, but Zhao Kuangyin said, "They have entrenched behind palisades because they fear us.

sentences.zh: 今吾眾不滿二千，若往擊之，則彼見吾眾寡矣；

translations.literal: Now our force is less than two thousand; if we go to attack them, then they will see how few we are;
translations.idiomatic: Our numbers are fewer than two thousand. If we go to them, they will see how weak we are;

sentences.zh: 不如俟其來而擊之，破之必矣！」

translations.literal: it would be better to wait until they come and then strike them—breaking them is certain!
translations.idiomatic: better to wait until they come to us and then strike—we will surely break them!"

sentences.zh: 居數日，唐出兵趣六合，太祖皇帝奮擊，大破之，殺獲近五千人，餘眾尚萬餘，走渡江，爭舟溺死者甚眾，於是唐之精卒盡矣。

translations.literal: After several days, the Tang army sallied toward Liuhe; the Taizu Emperor fought fiercely and routed them utterly, killing and capturing nearly five thousand; the remaining force still numbered more than ten thousand; they fled across the river; many drowned struggling for boats; and thus the Tang's crack troops were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later the Southern Tang army marched on Liuhe. Zhao Kuangyin met them with fierce assault and won a crushing victory, killing or capturing nearly five thousand. The remainder, still more than ten thousand strong, fled to the river; many drowned in the scramble for boats. With that, the Southern Tang's finest troops were spent.

sentences.zh: 是戰也，士卒有不致力者。

translations.literal: In this battle, some among the soldiers did not exert themselves fully.
translations.idiomatic: In this fight, some soldiers had held back.

sentences.zh: 太祖皇帝陽為督戰，以劍斫其皮笠。

translations.literal: The Taizu Emperor pretended to urge them into battle and struck their leather helmets with his sword.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Kuangyin, feigning the role of battle overseer, hacked at their leather helmets with his sword.

sentences.zh: 明日，遍閱其皮笠，有劍□亦者數十人，皆斬之，由是部兵莫敢不盡死，先是，唐主聞揚州失守，命四旁發兵取之。

translations.literal: The next day he inspected all their leather helmets; several dozen men bore sword marks; all were beheaded; from this the troops under his command dared not fail to fight to the death. Earlier, the Tang ruler, hearing that Yangzhou had fallen, ordered armies from all quarters to march and recover it.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he inspected every leather helmet in the unit; dozens bore sword marks—all were executed. Thereafter none in his command dared hold back in battle. Earlier, upon hearing that Yangzhou had been lost, the Southern Tang ruler had ordered troops summoned from every direction to retake it.

sentences.zh: 己卯，韓令坤奏敗楚州兵萬餘人於灣頭堰，獲漣州刺史秦進崇。

translations.literal: On the jimao day, Han Lingkun reported defeating more than ten thousand troops from Chuzhou at Wantou Weir and capturing Qin Jincong, prefect of Lianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao, Han Lingkun reported a victory over more than ten thousand enemy troops from Chuzhou at Wantou Weir, and the capture of Qin Jincong, prefect of Lianzhou.

sentences.zh: 張永德奏敗泗州兵萬餘人於曲溪堰。

translations.literal: Zhang Yongde reported defeating more than ten thousand troops from Sizhou at Quxi Weir.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yongde reported defeating more than ten thousand troops from Sizhou at Quxi Weir.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，以宣徽南院使向訓為淮南節度使兼沿江招討使。

translations.literal: On the bingxu day, Xiang Xun, commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat, was appointed military governor of Huainan and concurrently riverine campaign commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu, Xiang Xun of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat was made military governor of Huainan and concurrently commissioner for riverine operations.

sentences.zh: 渦口奏新作浮梁成。

translations.literal: Wokou reported that the newly built floating bridge had been completed.
translations.idiomatic: A dispatch from Wokou reported that the new floating bridge had been completed.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，帝自濠州如渦口。

translations.literal: On the dinghai day, the Emperor went from Haozhou to Wokou.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, the Emperor traveled from Haozhou to Wokou.

sentences.zh: 帝銳於進取，欲自至揚州，范質等以兵疲食少，泣諫而止。

translations.literal: The Emperor was keen on advancing and wished to go personally to Yangzhou; Fan Zhi and others, citing weary troops and scant provisions, wept in remonstrance and stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: Eager to press the advance, the Emperor wished to go in person to Yangzhou, but Fan Zhi and others dissuaded him with tearful remonstrance, citing exhausted troops and dwindling supplies.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗怒翰林學士竇儀，欲殺之，范質入救之。

translations.literal: The Emperor once grew angry at Hanlin Academician Dou Yi and wished to kill him; Fan Zhi entered to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: On one occasion the Emperor flew into a rage at Dou Yi, a Hanlin academician, and meant to put him to death; Fan Zhi intervened to save him.

sentences.zh: 帝望見，知其意，即起避之。

translations.literal: The Emperor saw him from afar, knew his intention, and immediately rose to avoid him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor saw Fan Zhi coming and, reading his purpose, immediately rose to avoid him.

sentences.zh: 質趨前伏地，叩頭諫曰：「儀罪不至死，臣為宰相，致陛下枉殺近臣，罪皆在臣。」

translations.literal: Zhi hurried forward, prostrated himself, and remonstrated, kowtowing: "Yi's offense does not warrant death. I am Prime Minister; if Your Majesty wrongly slays a close minister, the fault lies entirely with me."
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhi rushed forward, threw himself to the ground, and kowtowed in remonstrance: "Yi's fault does not deserve death. I serve as your Chancellor—if Your Majesty wrongly executes a court intimate, the blame is wholly mine."

sentences.zh: 繼之以泣。

translations.literal: He followed this with weeping.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke through tears.

sentences.zh: 帝意解，乃釋之。

translations.literal: The Emperor's anger eased, and he then released Yi.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's wrath softened, and he spared Yi.

sentences.zh: 北漢葬神武帝於交城北山，廟號世祖。

translations.literal: Northern Han buried Emperor Shenwu at the north mountain of Jiaocheng; his temple name was Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Han interred Emperor Shenwu on the northern hill at Jiaocheng, giving him the temple name Shizu.

sentences.zh: 五月，壬辰朔，以渦口為鎮淮軍。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the first day renchen, Wokou was established as Zhenhuai Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the first day of the month (renchen), Wokou was designated the Zhenhuai Army garrison.

sentences.zh: 丙申，唐永安節度使陳誨敗福州兵於南台江，俘斬千餘級。

translations.literal: On the bingshen day, Chen Hui, military governor of Yong'an of Tang, defeated Fuzhou troops at Nantai River, capturing and beheading more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, Chen Hui, military governor of Yong'an for the Southern Tang, routed Fuzhou troops on the Nantai River, killing and capturing more than a thousand.

sentences.zh: 唐主更命永安曰忠義軍。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler renamed Yong'an as the Loyal and Righteous Army.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Tang ruler redesignated the Yong'an command as the Loyal and Righteous Army.

sentences.zh: 誨，德誠之父也。

translations.literal: Hui was the father of Decheng.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hui was the father of Chen Decheng.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，帝留侍衛親軍都指揮使李重進等圍壽州，自渦口北歸，乙卯，至大梁。

translations.literal: On the wuxu day, the Emperor left Palace Guard commander-in-chief Li Chongjin and others to besiege Shouchun, and himself returned north from Wokou; on the yimao day, he reached Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, the Emperor left Li Chongjin, commander of the Palace Guard, and others to continue the siege of Shouchun and returned north from Wokou; on yimao he reached Daliang.

sentences.zh: 六月，壬申，赦淮南諸州系囚，除李氏非理賦役，事有不便於民者，委長吏以聞。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the renshen day, he amnestied prisoners held in the various prefectures of Huainan, abolished the Li family's unjust levies and corvee, and for matters inconvenient to the people, entrusted local officials to report upward.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on renshen, he granted amnesty to prisoners throughout Huainan, lifted the unjust taxes and corvee imposed under the Li regime, and ordered magistrates to report any remaining hardships to the throne.

sentences.zh: 侍衛步軍都指揮使、彰信節度使李繼勳營於壽州城南，唐劉仁贍伺繼勳無備，出兵擊之，殺士卒數百人，焚其攻具。

translations.literal: Li Jixun, commander of the Palace Guard infantry and military governor of Zhangxin, encamped south of Shouchun city; Liu Renshan of Tang, watching for Jixun's lack of preparedness, sallied forth and struck him, killing several hundred soldiers and burning his siege engines.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jixun, commander of the Palace Guard infantry and governor of Zhangxin, had encamped south of Shouchun. Liu Renshan of the Southern Tang, seizing a moment of laxity, sallied out and struck, killing several hundred men and burning the siege equipment.

sentences.zh: 唐駕部員外郎朱元因奏事論用兵方略，唐主以為能，命將兵復江北諸州。

translations.literal: Zhu Yuan, an outer-office secretary in the Tang Department of Imperial Transport, while submitting a memorial discussed military strategy; the Tang ruler deemed him capable and ordered him to lead troops to recover the various prefectures north of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yuan, an outer-office secretary in the Southern Tang transport bureau, discussed military strategy while presenting a memorial; the Southern Tang ruler judged him capable and entrusted him with recovering the prefectures north of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，辛卯朔，以周行逢為武平節度使，制置武安、靜江等軍事。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the first day xinmao, Zhou Xingfeng was appointed military governor of Wuping and given charge over military affairs of Wu'an, Jingjiang, and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on the first day (xinmao), Zhou Xingfeng was made military governor of Wuping with authority over military affairs in Wu'an, Jingjiang, and neighboring commands.

sentences.zh: 行逢既兼總湖、湘，乃矯前人之弊，留心民事，悉除馬氏橫賦，貪吏猾民為民害者皆去之，擇廉平吏為刺史、縣令。

translations.literal: Once Xingfeng had come to oversee Hunan and the Xiang region together, he corrected the abuses of his predecessors, attended to civil affairs, entirely abolished the Ma clan's exorbitant levies, removed greedy officials and cunning commoners who harmed the people, and selected upright and fair officials as prefects and magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: With Hunan and the Xiang region under his unified command, Zhou Xingfeng corrected the abuses of those who came before him, turned his mind to the people's welfare, abolished the Ma family's crushing levies, purged greedy officials and predatory locals, and appointed honest, fair men as prefects and magistrates.

sentences.zh: 朗州民、夷雜居，劉言，王逵舊將卒多驕橫，行逢壹以法治之，無所寬假，眾怨懟且懼。

translations.literal: In Langzhou Han and tribal peoples lived mixed together; many of the old soldiers and officers of Liu Yan and Wang Kui were arrogant and overbearing; Xingfeng applied the law uniformly without any leniency; the multitude both resented and feared.
translations.idiomatic: In Langzhou, Han settlers and tribal peoples lived side by side, and many veteran officers and men of Liu Yan and Wang Kui's faction remained proud and violent. Zhou Xingfeng enforced the law without favor or lenience; the men grumbled but also feared him.

sentences.zh: 有大將與其黨十餘人謀作亂，行逢知之，大會諸將，於座中擒之。

translations.literal: A major general and more than ten of his partisans plotted rebellion; Xingfeng learned of it, convened a great assembly of generals, and seized them in their seats.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that a senior general and a dozen of his followers were plotting rebellion, Zhou Xingfeng summoned the commanders to a grand assembly and seized the conspirators right in their seats.

sentences.zh: 數曰：「吾惡衣糲食，充實府庫，正為汝曹，何負而反！

translations.literal: He reproached them, saying: "I wear coarse clothes and eat plain food and fill the treasury—all for your sake—what have I failed in that you rebel!
translations.idiomatic: He upbraided them: "I wear coarse cloth and eat plain fare and fill the treasury for your sake—what wrong have I done you that you turn against me!

sentences.zh: 今日之會，與汝訣也！」

translations.literal: Today's gathering is my parting with you!
translations.idiomatic: This assembly is my farewell to you!"

sentences.zh: 立撾殺之，座上股慄。

translations.literal: He immediately had them beaten to death; those in their seats trembled in their thighs.
translations.idiomatic: He had them beaten to death on the spot; every man at the table trembled.

sentences.zh: 行逢曰：「諸君無罪，皆宜自安。」

translations.literal: Xingfeng said: "You gentlemen are guiltless and should all rest at ease."
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xingfeng then said, "The rest of you are innocent—put your minds at ease."

sentences.zh: 樂飲而罷。

translations.literal: They drank merrily and the meeting ended.
translations.idiomatic: They drank on in relief, and the gathering adjourned.

sentences.zh: 行逢多計數，善發隱伏，將卒有謀亂及叛亡者，行逢必先覺，擒殺之，所部凜然。

translations.literal: Xingfeng had many stratagems and was skilled at uncovering hidden plots; whenever officers or soldiers plotted rebellion or fled in desertion, Xingfeng always detected it first, seized and killed them; his subordinates were awestruck.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xingfeng was wily and skilled at uncovering hidden plots. Any officer or soldier who conspired or deserted was found out and executed before the deed could be done; his command stood in awe of him.

sentences.zh: 然性猜忍，常散遣人密詗諸州事，其之邵州者，無事可覆命，但言刺史劉光委多宴飲。

translations.literal: Yet by nature he was suspicious and ruthless; he often dispatched people in secret to investigate affairs in the various prefectures; one sent to Shaozhou had nothing of substance to report back, and only said that Prefect Liu Guangwei indulged in frequent feasting and drinking.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was suspicious and cruel by nature, and habitually sent agents to spy on affairs in the prefectures. One agent returned from Shaozhou with nothing substantial to report except that Prefect Liu Guangwei held frequent banquets.

sentences.zh: 行逢曰：「光委數聚飲，欲謀我邪！」

translations.literal: Xingfeng said: "Guangwei repeatedly gathers to drink—is he plotting against me!
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xingfeng said, "Guangwei holds feast after feast—does he mean to plot against me?"

sentences.zh: 即召還，殺之。

translations.literal: He immediately summoned Guangwei back and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Liu Guangwei back at once and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 親衛指揮使、衡州刺史張文表恐獲罪，求歸治所，行逢許之。

translations.literal: Zhang Wenbiao, commander of the personal guard and prefect of Hengzhou, feared being punished, requested to return to his post, and Xingfeng granted this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wenbiao, commander of the personal guard and prefect of Hengzhou, fearful of falling under suspicion, asked leave to return to his post; Zhou Xingfeng allowed it.

sentences.zh: 文表歲時饋獻甚厚，及謹事左右，由是得免。

translations.literal: Wenbiao every year made lavish presents, and moreover served Xingfeng's attendants scrupulously; thereby he escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wenbiao sent lavish seasonal gifts and cultivated Zhou Xingfeng's inner circle with care, and so escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 行逢妻鄖國夫人鄧氏，陋而剛決，善治生，嘗諫行逢用法太嚴，人無親附者。

translations.literal: Xingfeng's wife, Lady Deng, Duchess of Yun, was plain in appearance yet resolute; skilled at managing household affairs; she once remonstrated that Xingfeng's enforcement of law was too harsh and that people had no one to whom they felt close attachment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xingfeng's wife, Lady Deng, Duchess of Yun, was plain of face but firm of will and skilled at managing estates. She once warned him that his law was too harsh and that the people had no warmth toward him.

sentences.zh: 行逢怒曰：「汝婦人何知！」

translations.literal: Xingfeng angrily said: "What does a woman like you know!
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xingfeng snapped, "What would a woman know of such things!"

sentences.zh: 鄧氏不悅，因請之村墅視田園，遂不復歸府捨。

translations.literal: Lady Deng was displeased; she requested to go to the country estate to inspect the fields and gardens, and thereafter did not return to the official residence.
translations.idiomatic: Offended, Lady Deng asked to retire to their country estate to oversee the fields, and did not return to the prefectural residence.

sentences.zh: 行逢屢遣人迎之，不至。

translations.literal: Xingfeng repeatedly sent people to welcome her back; she would not come.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xingfeng sent messengers again and again to bring her home, but she refused to return.

sentences.zh: 一旦，自帥僮僕來輸稅，行逢就見之，曰：「吾為節度使，夫人何自苦如此！」

translations.literal: One day she herself led servants to come and pay taxes; Xingfeng went to see her and said: "I am military governor—why does my lady torment herself so!
translations.idiomatic: One day she came in person with her servants to deliver the tax payment. Zhou Xingfeng went out to meet her and said, "I am the military governor—why must you burden yourself like this?"

sentences.zh: 鄧氏曰：「稅，官物也。

translations.literal: Lady Deng said: "Taxes are the state's property.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Deng replied, "Taxes belong to the state.

sentences.zh: 公為節度使，不先輸稅，何以率下！

translations.literal: You serve as military governor; if you do not pay taxes first, how can you lead those below!
translations.idiomatic: As military governor, if you do not pay your taxes first, how can you expect your subordinates to follow your example?

sentences.zh: 且獨不記為裡正代人輸稅以免楚撻時邪？」

translations.literal: Moreover, do you alone not remember when, as village head, you paid taxes on others' behalf to avoid the cudgel's beating?
translations.idiomatic: Have you forgotten when you were village head and paid others' taxes yourself to spare them the flogging?"

sentences.zh: 行逢欲與之歸，不可，曰：「公誅殺太過，常恐一旦有變，村墅易為逃匿耳。」

translations.literal: Xingfeng wished to return with her; she would not consent, saying: "Your lordship executes too many; I constantly fear that if change comes one day, a country estate is easier for hiding escape.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xingfeng urged her to come home, but she refused, saying, "You have killed too many. I live in constant fear of sudden upheaval—a country estate is easier to vanish into."

sentences.zh: 行逢慚怒，其僚屬曰：「夫人言直，公宜納之。」

translations.literal: Xingfeng felt shamed and angry; his staff said: "The lady speaks bluntly; your lordship should accept it."
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xingfeng flushed with shame and anger. His staff said, "My lord, the lady speaks plainly—you would do well to heed her."

sentences.zh: 行逢婿唐德求補吏，行逢曰：「汝才不堪為吏，吾今私汝則可矣。

translations.literal: Xingfeng's son-in-law Tang De asked to be appointed to an office; Xingfeng said: "Your talent is unfit for office; I could favor you privately now.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xingfeng's son-in-law Tang De asked for a government post. Zhou Xingfeng said, "Your talents are not equal to office. I could show you private favor now.

sentences.zh: 汝居官無狀，吾不敢以法貸汝，則親戚之恩絕矣。」

translations.literal: If you hold office without merit, I dare not exempt you by law, and then the bond of kinship is severed."
translations.idiomatic: But if you served without distinction, I could not spare you the law—and then the tie of kinship would be broken."

sentences.zh: 與之耕牛、農具而遣之。

translations.literal: He gave him draft oxen and farm tools and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: He gave him draft oxen and farm tools and sent him on his way.

sentences.zh: 行逢少時嘗坐事黥，隸辰州銅坑，或說行逢：「公面有文，恐為朝廷使者所嗤，請以藥滅之。」

translations.literal: In his youth Xingfeng had once been tattooed for an offense and assigned to the copper mines of Chenzhou; someone advised Xingfeng: "Your lordship's face bears marks; I fear court envoys will mock you—please use medicine to erase them."
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Zhou Xingfeng had been tattooed for a crime and sent to labor in the Chenzhou copper mines. Someone urged him: "Your face bears the mark; court envoys may ridicule you—let medicine erase it."

sentences.zh: 行逢曰：「吾聞漢有黥布，不害為英雄，吾何恥焉！」

translations.literal: Xingfeng said: "I have heard that in Han there was Qing Bu; it did not prevent him from being a hero—why should I be ashamed!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xingfeng said, "I have heard that in Han there was Qing Bu—the tattoo did not keep him from being a hero. Why should I be ashamed?"

sentences.zh: 自劉言、王逵以來，屢舉兵，將吏積功及所羈縻蠻夷，檢校官至三公者以千數。

translations.literal: Since Liu Yan and Wang Kui, armies had been raised repeatedly; officers and men who accumulated merit, together with subjugated tribal peoples, numbered in the thousands who held honorary posts reaching the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Since the days of Liu Yan and Wang Kui, war had been raised again and again; officers and men who had earned merit, together with subjugated tribal peoples, numbered in the thousands holding honorary ranks as high as the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 前天策府學士徐仲雅，自馬希廣之廢，杜門不仕，行逢慕之，署節度判官。

translations.literal: The former Tiancefujun academician Xu Zhongya, since Ma Xiguang's deposition, had shut his doors and refused office; Xingfeng admired him and appointed him military governor's adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhongya, a former academician of the Tiancefujun, had lived in seclusion since Ma Xiguang's fall. Zhou Xingfeng admired him and named him adjutant to the military governor.

sentences.zh: 仲雅曰：「行逢昔趨事我，奈何為之幕吏！」

translations.literal: Zhongya said: "Xingfeng once attended upon me—how can I serve as his staff officer!
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhongya said, "Xingfeng once waited on me in person—how can I become his staff officer?"

sentences.zh: 辭疾不至。

translations.literal: He declined on grounds of illness and did not come.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness and refused to come.

sentences.zh: 行逢迫脅固召之，面授文牒，終辭不取，行逢怒，放之邵州，既而召還。

translations.literal: Xingfeng coerced and pressed him, summoning him by force; he personally handed him the commission, but Zhongya ultimately refused to accept it; Xingfeng was angry and sent him to Shaozhou, then later summoned him back.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xingfeng pressed him relentlessly and summoned him by force, personally handing him the commission; Xu Zhongya still refused to accept it. Xingfeng in anger sent him to Shaozhou, then later recalled him.

sentences.zh: 會行逢生日，諸道各遣使致賀，行逢有矜色，謂仲雅曰：「自吾兼鎮三府，四鄰亦畏我乎？」

translations.literal: It happened to be Xingfeng's birthday; each circuit sent envoys to offer congratulations; Xingfeng wore a proud look and said to Zhongya: "Since I have held three commands together, do the neighboring circuits also fear me?
translations.idiomatic: On Zhou Xingfeng's birthday, envoys from every circuit arrived with congratulations. Pleased with himself, he asked Xu Zhongya, "Since I have held three commands at once, do our neighbors fear me as well?"

sentences.zh: 仲雅曰：「侍中境內，彌天太保，遍地司空，四鄰那得不畏！」

translations.literal: Zhongya said: "Within the Vice Grand Councilor's territory, Grand Preceptors fill the sky and Honorary Inspectors-General cover the ground—how could the neighbors not fear!
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhongya replied, "Within your borders, Grand Preceptors fill the sky and Honorary Inspectors-General cover the earth—how could the neighbors not fear you?"

sentences.zh: 行逢復放之邵州，竟不能屈。

translations.literal: Xingfeng again sent him to Shaozhou and ultimately could not break him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xingfeng sent him back to Shaozhou again and never broke his will.

sentences.zh: 有僧仁及，為行逢所信任，軍府事皆預之，亦加檢校司空，娶數妻，出入導從如王公。

translations.literal: There was a monk, Renji, whom Xingfeng trusted; he took part in all military headquarters affairs, was also given the honorary post of Inspector-General of Works, took several wives, and went in and out with escorts like a prince or duke.
translations.idiomatic: A monk named Renji enjoyed Zhou Xingfeng's trust, took part in every affair of the military headquarters, held the honorary rank of Inspector-General of Works, kept several wives, and went abroad with a retinue fit for a prince.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，宣懿皇后符氏殂。

translations.literal: On the xinhai day, Empress Xuanyi, nee Fu, passed away.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, Empress Xuanyi, of the Fu clan, died.

sentences.zh: 唐將朱元取舒州，刺史郭令圖棄城走。

translations.literal: The Tang general Zhu Yuan took Shuzhou; Prefect Guo Lingtu abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Tang general Zhu Yuan took Shuzhou; Prefect Guo Lingtu abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 李平取蘄州。

translations.literal: Li Ping took Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ping took Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 唐主以元為舒州團練使，平為蘄州刺史。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler made Yuan regimental commander of Shuzhou and Ping prefect of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Tang ruler made Zhu Yuan regimental commander of Shuzhou and Li Ping prefect of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 元又取和州。

translations.literal: Yuan also took Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yuan also took Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 初，唐人以茶鹽強民而徵其粟帛，謂之博徵，又興營田於淮南，民甚苦之。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Tang people had forced the people with tea and salt levies and collected grain and cloth from them, calling it forced exchange; they also established military farms in Huainan, and the people suffered greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Southern Tang had coerced the people with tea and salt monopolies and collected grain and cloth in what they called forced exchange, and they established military farms across Huainan; the people suffered greatly.

sentences.zh: 及周師至，爭奉牛酒迎勞。

translations.literal: When Zhou armies arrived, the people competed to offer oxen and wine to welcome and refresh them.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou armies arrived, the people vied to bring oxen and wine to welcome and refresh them.

sentences.zh: 而將帥不之恤，專事俘掠，視民如土芥。

translations.literal: Yet the generals did not care for them and devoted themselves solely to capture and plunder, treating the people like weeds.
translations.idiomatic: But the commanders paid them no heed and devoted themselves to capture and plunder, treating the people like weeds.

sentences.zh: 民皆失望，相聚山澤，立堡壁自固，操農器為兵，積紙為甲，時人謂之「白甲軍」。

translations.literal: The people all lost hope, gathered in mountains and marshes, built fortresses to protect themselves, took up farm tools as weapons, piled paper as armor, and people of the time called them the "White Armor Army."
translations.idiomatic: “The people lost all hope, fled into hills and marshes, built fortresses for protection, took up farm tools as weapons and piled paper into armor; contemporaries called them the White Armor Army.”

sentences.zh: 周兵討之，屢為所敗，先所得唐諸州，多復為唐有。

translations.literal: Zhou troops campaigned against them and were repeatedly defeated by them; the Tang prefectures previously taken were largely recovered by Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou troops campaigned against them and were repeatedly beaten; many of the Southern Tang prefectures already taken were lost again to the Tang.

sentences.zh: 唐之援兵營於紫金山，與壽春城中烽火相應。

translations.literal: Tang relief troops encamped at Purple Gold Mountain, coordinating with beacon fires in Shouchun city.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Tang relief troops encamped on Purple Gold Mountain, coordinating with beacon fires in Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 淮南節度使向訓奏請以廣陵之兵並力攻壽春，俟克城，更圖進取，詔許之。

translations.literal: The Huainan military governor Xiang Xun memorialized requesting that the troops from Guangling join forces to attack Shouchun, and after the city was taken, to plan further advance; the edict granted this.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Xun, military governor of Huainan, memorialized asking that the forces from Guangling combine to assault Shouchun and, once the city fell, plan the next advance; the throne approved.

sentences.zh: 訓封府庫以授揚州主者，命揚州牙將分部按行城中，秋毫不犯，揚州民感悅，軍還，或負糗□以送之。

translations.literal: Xun sealed the treasury and handed it to the Yangzhou custodian, ordered Yangzhou military officers to patrol the city in sections without violating the slightest thing; the people of Yangzhou were moved and pleased; when the army withdrew, some carried dry rations on their backs to see them off.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Xun sealed the treasury and entrusted it to Yangzhou's custodian, ordered the garrison officers to patrol the city ward by ward without the slightest violation; the people of Yangzhou were deeply moved. When the army withdrew, some shouldered dry provisions to see them off.

sentences.zh: 滁州守將亦棄城去，皆引兵趣壽春。

translations.literal: The defending general of Chuzhou also abandoned the city and left; all led troops toward Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison commander of Chuzhou also abandoned his post; all marched their troops toward Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 唐諸將請據險以邀周師，宋齊丘曰：「如此，則怨益深，不如縱之，以德於敵，則兵易解也。」

translations.literal: Tang generals asked to hold strategic passes and intercept Zhou forces. Song Qiuqiu said: "If we do this, resentment will only deepen. Better to let them go and show virtue toward the enemy—then the army may more easily be withdrawn."
translations.idiomatic: Southern Tang generals urged holding the defiles to ambush the Zhou army. Song Qiuqiu said, "That would only deepen their hatred. Better to let them withdraw and treat the enemy with forbearance—the siege may then be lifted more easily."

sentences.zh: 乃命諸將各自守，毋得擅出擊周兵。

translations.literal: He then ordered the generals each to hold their positions and not to attack Zhou troops on their own authority.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered every general to hold his post and not launch unauthorized attacks on Zhou forces.

sentences.zh: 由是壽春之圍益急。

translations.literal: Accordingly the siege of Shouchun grew tighter.
translations.idiomatic: As a result the siege of Shouchun tightened further.

sentences.zh: 齊王景達軍於濠州，遙為壽州聲援，軍政皆出於陳覺，景達署紙尾而已。

translations.literal: Prince of Qi Jing Da encamped at Haozhou, providing distant support for Shouzhou. All military and civil affairs came from Chen Jue; Jing Da merely signed at the bottom of documents.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qi Jing Da camped at Haozhou, lending distant support to Shou prefecture. Chen Jue controlled all military and civil affairs; Jing Da only appended his signature at the foot of each document.

sentences.zh: 擁兵五萬，無決戰意，將吏畏覺，無敢言者。

translations.literal: He had fifty thousand troops but no will for a decisive battle. Officers and officials feared Chen Jue; none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded fifty thousand men but had no appetite for a pitched battle. Officers and staff feared Chen Jue, and none dared object.

sentences.zh: 八月，戊辰，端明殿學士王朴、司天少監王處訥撰《顯德欽天曆》，上之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on wuchen, Hanlin academician Wang Pu and Assistant Director of the Astronomical Bureau Wang Chune compiled the Xiande Qintian Calendar and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the wuchen day, Wang Pu, academician of the Hall of Duanming, and Wang Chune, assistant director of the Astronomical Bureau, compiled the Xiande Qintian Calendar and submitted it.

sentences.zh: 詔自來歲行之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered it to take effect from the following year.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered its adoption beginning the next year.

sentences.zh: 殿前都指揮使、義成節度使張永德屯下蔡，唐將林仁肇以水陸軍援壽春。

translations.literal: Commander of the Palace Front Corps and Yicheng military governor Zhang Yongde encamped at Xiaqi. Tang general Lin Renzhao came by land and water to relieve Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yongde, commander of the Palace Front Corps and military governor of Yicheng, encamped at Xiaqi. Southern Tang general Lin Renzhao marched by land and water to relieve Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 永德與之戰，仁肇以船實薪芻，因風縱火，欲焚下蔡浮梁，俄而風回，唐兵敗退。

translations.literal: Zhang Yongde fought him. Lin Renzhao loaded boats with firewood and fodder, and riding the wind set them afire intending to burn the pontoon bridge at Xiaqi; but soon the wind shifted back and Tang troops were defeated and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yongde gave battle. Lin Renzhao filled boats with kindling and fodder, then sent them blazing downwind toward the Xiaqi pontoon bridge; the wind suddenly turned, and the Tang force was beaten and driven off.

sentences.zh: 永德為鐵綆千餘尺，距浮梁十餘步，橫絕淮流，系以巨木，由是唐兵不能近。

translations.literal: Zhang Yongde had iron chains more than a thousand chi long laid ten-odd paces from the pontoon bridge, stretching across the Huai current and tied to huge logs—thus Tang troops could not approach.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yongde stretched iron chains more than a thousand feet long across the Huai ten-odd paces from the pontoon bridge, anchoring them to great logs, so Tang ships could not get near.

sentences.zh: 九月，丙午，以端明殿學士、左散騎常侍、權知開封府事王朴為戶部侍郎，充樞密副使。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on bingwu, Wang Pu, Hanlin academician, Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalier for Attending Affairs, and acting prefect of Kaifeng, was made Vice Minister of Revenue and Deputy Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the bingwu day, Wang Pu—Hanlin academician, left regular attendant, and acting prefect of Kaifeng—was appointed vice minister of revenue and deputy commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，癸酉，李重進奏唐人寇盛唐，鐵騎都指揮使王彥升等擊破之，斬首三千餘級。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on guiyou, Li Chongjin reported that Tang men raided Sheng Tang. Iron Cavalry Commander Wang Yansheng and others routed them and took more than three thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on the guiyou day, Li Chongjin reported a Tang raid on Sheng Tang. Wang Yansheng, commander of the Iron Cavalry, and others smashed the enemy and took more than three thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 彥升，蜀人也。

translations.literal: Yansheng was a man of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Yansheng was from Shu.

sentences.zh: 丙子，上謂侍臣：「近朝徵斂穀帛，多不俟收穫、紡績之畢。」

translations.literal: On bingzi the Emperor told his attendants: "Recently the collection of grain and cloth has often not waited until harvest and spinning were complete."
translations.idiomatic: On the bingzi day, Later Zhou Emperor Shizong told his attendants, "Lately the levy of grain and cloth has often come before the harvest and the spinning are finished."

sentences.zh: 乃詔三司，自今夏稅以六月，秋稅以十月起徵，民間便之。

translations.literal: He then ordered the Three Departments that summer tax would be levied from the sixth month and autumn tax from the tenth month; the people found this convenient.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered the Three Departments to begin summer tax in the sixth month and autumn tax in the tenth; the people welcomed the change.

sentences.zh: 山南東道節度使、守太尉兼中書令安審琦鎮襄州十餘年，至是入朝，除守太師，遣還鎮。

translations.literal: An Shenqi, Military Governor of Shannan East Circuit, Defender Grand Preceptor and concurrent Grand Chancellor, had governed Xiangzhou for more than ten years. Now he came to court, was appointed Defender Grand Mentor, and sent back to his post.
translations.idiomatic: An Shenqi, military governor of Shannan East Circuit, defender grand preceptor and concurrent grand chancellor, had held Xiangzhou for more than ten years. He now came to court, was promoted to defender grand mentor, and returned to his command.

sentences.zh: 既行，上問宰相：「卿曹送之乎？」

translations.literal: After he departed, the Emperor asked the chief ministers: "Did you see him off?"
translations.idiomatic: After An Shenqi left, Later Zhou Emperor Shizong asked the chief ministers, "Did you escort him?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「送至城南，審琦深感聖恩。」

translations.literal: They replied: "We saw him off as far as the south of the city. Shenqi was deeply grateful for imperial favor."
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "We saw him off to the south of the city. Shenqi was deeply moved by Your Majesty's grace."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「近朝多不以誠信待諸侯，諸侯雖有欲效忠節者，其道無由。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Recently the court has often not treated regional lords with sincerity and trust. Though a lord might wish to serve with loyalty, he has no way to do so.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "In recent times the throne has too often dealt with regional lords without sincerity. Even when a lord wished to prove his loyalty, he had no path to do so.

sentences.zh: 王者但能毋失其信，何患諸侯不歸心哉！」

translations.literal: If a king simply does not break his word, what worry is there that lords will not give him their hearts!"
translations.idiomatic: If a sovereign simply keeps faith, why fear that lords will not give him their hearts?"

sentences.zh: 壬午，張永德奏敗唐兵於下蔡。

translations.literal: On renwu, Zhang Yongde reported defeating Tang troops at Xiaqi.
translations.idiomatic: On the renwu day, Zhang Yongde reported a victory over Tang forces at Xiaqi.

sentences.zh: 是時唐復以水軍攻永德，永德夜令善游者沒其船下，縻以鐵鎖，縱兵擊之，船不得進退，溺死者甚眾。

translations.literal: At this time Tang again attacked Yongde with a naval force. Yongde by night ordered skilled swimmers to dive beneath their boats and bind them with iron chains, then sent troops to attack; the boats could neither advance nor retreat, and very many drowned.
