translations.idiomatic: Tang warships again assailed Yongde. By night he sent expert swimmers beneath the enemy hulls to lash them with iron chains, then struck with his troops; trapped, the ships could neither advance nor retreat, and a great many men drowned.

sentences.zh: 永德解金帶以賞善游者。

translations.literal: Yongde removed his gold belt to reward the skilled swimmers.
translations.idiomatic: Yongde took off his gold belt and gave it to the swimmers as a reward.

sentences.zh: 甲申，以太祖皇帝為定國節度使兼殿前都指揮使。

translations.literal: On jiashen, Zhao Kuangyin was made military governor of Dingguo and concurrent commander of the Palace Front Corps.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiashen day, Zhao Kuangyin was appointed military governor of Dingguo and concurrent commander of the Palace Front Corps.

sentences.zh: 太祖皇帝表渭州軍事判官趙普為節度推官。

translations.literal: Zhao Kuangyin memorialized recommending Zhao Pu, military affairs judge of Weizhou, as administrative aide of the military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Kuangyin recommended Zhao Pu, military affairs judge at Weizhou, for appointment as the governor's administrative aide.

sentences.zh: 張永德與李重進不相悅，永德密表重進有二心，帝不之信。

translations.literal: Zhang Yongde and Li Chongjin were on bad terms. Yongde secretly memorialized that Chongjin had divided loyalties; the Emperor did not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yongde and Li Chongjin disliked each other. Yongde secretly reported that Chongjin was disloyal, but Later Zhou Emperor Shizong did not credit it.

sentences.zh: 時二將各擁重兵，眾心憂恐。

translations.literal: At the time the two generals each commanded large armies, and popular sentiment was anxious and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Both generals now held heavy commands, and unease spread through the ranks.

sentences.zh: 重進一日單騎詣永德營，從容宴飲，謂永德曰：「吾與公幸以肺腑俱為將帥，奚相疑若此之深邪？」

translations.literal: One day Chongjin came alone on horseback to Yongde's camp, and over a leisurely banquet said to Yongde: "You and I are fortunate to serve as commanders bound by kinship—why such deep mutual suspicion?"
translations.idiomatic: One day Li Chongjin rode alone to Zhang Yongde's camp. Over a relaxed banquet he said, "We are kinsmen who share the same command—why such deep mistrust?"

sentences.zh: 永德意乃解，眾心亦安。

translations.literal: Yongde's suspicions were then resolved, and popular sentiment was also calmed.
translations.idiomatic: Yongde's doubts dissolved, and the army's fears eased.

sentences.zh: 唐主聞之，以蠟書遺重進，誘以厚利。

translations.literal: When the Southern Tang ruler heard of this, he sent Chongjin a letter sealed in wax, tempting him with rich rewards.
translations.idiomatic: When the Southern Tang ruler learned of the reconciliation, he sent Li Chongjin a wax-sealed letter promising lavish rewards.

sentences.zh: 其書皆謗毀及反間之語，重進奏之。

translations.literal: The letter contained only slander and words of subversion; Chongjin reported it.
translations.idiomatic: The message was filled with abuse and sedition; Chongjin forwarded it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 初，唐使者孫晟、鐘謨從帝至大梁，帝待之甚厚，每朝會，班於中書省官之後。

translations.literal: Earlier, Tang envoys Sun Sheng and Zhong Mo had followed the Emperor to Daliang. The Emperor treated them very generously; at each court assembly they were ranked after the officials of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Southern Tang envoys Sun Sheng and Zhong Mo had accompanied Later Zhou Emperor Shizong to Daliang. He treated them with great honor; at every court session they were placed after the Secretariat officials.

sentences.zh: 時召見，飲以醇酒，問以唐事。

translations.literal: He would summon them and give them fine wine, questioning them about Tang affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He often summoned them, plied them with strong wine, and questioned them about Tang affairs.

sentences.zh: 晟但言「唐主畏陛下神武，事陛下無二心。」

translations.literal: Sheng would only say: "The Tang ruler fears Your Majesty's divine martial prowess and serves Your Majesty without a second thought."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng would say only, "The Southern Tang ruler stands in awe of Your Majesty's might and serves you with undivided loyalty."

sentences.zh: 及得唐蠟書，帝大怒，召晟，責以所對不實。

translations.literal: When the Tang wax-sealed letter was obtained, the Emperor was greatly angered, summoned Sheng, and rebuked him for answering untruthfully.
translations.idiomatic: When the wax-sealed Tang letter arrived, the Emperor flew into a rage, summoned Sun Sheng, and accused him of lying.

sentences.zh: 晟正色抗辭，請死而已。

translations.literal: Sheng with stern countenance answered forcefully, asking only to die.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng answered with stern dignity, asking only to die.

sentences.zh: 問以唐虛實，默不對。

translations.literal: Asked about Tang's true strength and weakness, he was silent and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Questioned about Tang's real condition, he remained silent.

sentences.zh: 十一月，乙巳，帝命都承旨曹翰送晟於右軍巡院，更以帝意問之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on yisi, the Emperor ordered Chief Secretariat recipient Cao Han to escort Sheng to the Right Army Inspection Office and question him again according to the Emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the yisi day, the Emperor ordered Cao Han, chief recipient of the Secretariat, to take Sun Sheng to the Right Army Inspection Office and press him once more.

sentences.zh: 翰與之飲酒數行，從容問之，晟終不言。

translations.literal: Han drank several rounds with him and questioned him at ease; Sheng in the end said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Han shared several cups with him and questioned him gently; Sun Sheng still would not speak.

sentences.zh: 翰乃謂曰：「有敕，賜相公死。」

translations.literal: Han then said to him: "There is an edict granting the Chancellor death."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Han then said, "There is an edict sentencing you to death, Chancellor."

sentences.zh: 晟神色怡然，索鞋笏，整衣冠，南向拜曰：「臣謹以死報國！」

translations.literal: Sheng's expression was calm and pleased. He asked for shoes and tablet, straightened his robes and cap, bowed facing south and said: "Your servant respectfully dies to repay the state!"
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng looked serene. He asked for his shoes and court tablet, straightened his robes, bowed toward the south, and said, "I die gladly in service to my country!"

sentences.zh: 乃就刑。

translations.literal: He then submitted to execution.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to his death.

sentences.zh: 並從者百餘人皆殺之，貶鐘謨耀州司馬。

translations.literal: More than a hundred of his attendants were also killed; Zhong Mo was demoted to defender marshal of Yao prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred of his followers were executed as well; Zhong Mo was demoted to defender marshal of Yao prefecture.

sentences.zh: 既而帝憐晟忠節，悔殺之，召謨，拜衛尉少卿。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the Emperor pitied Sheng's loyalty and regretted killing him; he summoned Mo and appointed him Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Regalia.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Emperor came to admire Sun Sheng's loyalty and regretted his death; he recalled Zhong Mo and made him vice director of the Court of Imperial Regalia.

sentences.zh: 帝召華山隱士真源陳摶，問以飛升、黃白之術。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned Chen Tuan, a recluse of Mount Hua from Zhenyuan, and questioned him about techniques of ascension and transmutation of metals.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhou Emperor Shizong summoned Chen Tuan, a hermit of Mount Hua from Zhenyuan, and asked him about immortality and the alchemical arts.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「陛下為天子，當以治天下為務，安用此為！」

translations.literal: He replied: "Your Majesty is Son of Heaven—You should make governing the realm Your task. What use is this!"
translations.idiomatic: Chen Tuan answered, "Your Majesty is Son of Heaven; your business is to govern the realm. What need have you of such things?"

sentences.zh: 戊申，遣還山，詔州縣長吏常存問之。

translations.literal: On wushen he was sent back to the mountain; an edict ordered the prefectural and county magistrates to inquire after him regularly.
translations.idiomatic: On the wushen day he was sent back to the mountain, with orders that local magistrates should look in on him regularly.

sentences.zh: 十二月，壬申，以張永德為殿前都點檢。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on renshen, Zhang Yongde was made Chief Inspector of the Palace Front Corps.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the renshen day, Zhang Yongde was appointed chief inspector of the Palace Front Corps.

sentences.zh: 分命中使發陳、蔡、宋、亳、穎、兗、曹、單等州丁夫數萬城下蔡。

translations.literal: Separately the Emperor ordered palace envoys to mobilize tens of thousands of corvée laborers from Chen, Cai, Song, Bo, Ying, Yan, Cao, Shan, and other prefectures to fortify Xiaqi.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor dispatched palace envoys to levy tens of thousands of laborers from Chen, Cai, Song, Bo, Ying, Yan, Cao, Shan, and neighboring prefectures to build fortifications at Xiaqi.

sentences.zh: 是歲，唐主詔淮南營田害民尤甚者罷之。

translations.literal: That year the Southern Tang ruler ordered that the most harmful Huainan garrison-farm projects be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Southern Tang ruler abolished the Huainan garrison farms that had most oppressed the people.

sentences.zh: 遣兵部郎中陳處堯持重幣，浮海如契丹乞兵。

translations.literal: He sent Chen Chuyao, director of the Ministry of War, bearing heavy gifts to cross the sea to the Khitan and beg for troops.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Chen Chuyao of the Ministry of War, bearing rich gifts, to sail to the Khitan and request troops.

sentences.zh: 契丹不能為之出兵，而留處堯不遣。

translations.literal: The Khitan could not send troops for him but detained Chuyao and would not release him.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan could not furnish an army, but they kept Chen Chuyao and refused to let him return.

sentences.zh: 處堯剛直有口辯，久之，忿懟，數面責契丹主，契丹主亦不之罪也。

translations.literal: Chuyao was upright and eloquent. After a long time he grew resentful and repeatedly rebuked the Khitan ruler to his face; the Khitan ruler also did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Chuyao was blunt and quick-tongued. In time he grew furious and repeatedly upbraided the Khitan ruler to his face; the Khitan ruler never punished him.

sentences.zh: 蜀陵、榮州獠叛，弓箭庫使趙季文討平之。

translations.literal: The Liao and Rong prefecture Liao tribes rebelled in Shu; Zhao Jiwen, commissioner of the Bow and Arrow Storehouse, suppressed and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao tribes of Ling and Rong prefectures in Shu rebelled; Zhao Jiwen, commissioner of the Bow and Arrow Storehouse, put down the revolt.

sentences.zh: 吳越王弘俶括境內民捕，勞擾頗多，判明州錢弘億手疏切諫，罷之。

translations.literal: Qian Hongchu, King of Wuyue, conscripted the people within his borders to hunt birds, causing much labor and disturbance. Qian Hongyi, administrator of Ming prefecture, memorialized forcefully in protest, and the practice was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: King Qian Hongchu of Wuyue conscripted people throughout his realm to hunt birds, causing widespread hardship. Qian Hongyi, administrator of Ming prefecture, submitted a blunt memorial of protest, and the practice was halted.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，己丑朔，北漢大赦，改元天會。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the jichou new moon, Northern Han proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Tianhui.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the new moon of jichou, Northern Han proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Tianhui.

sentences.zh: 以翰林學士衛融為中書侍郎、同平章事，內客省使段恆為樞密使。

translations.literal: Hanlin academician Wei Rong was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and concurrent Grand Chancellor; Inner Reception Commissioner Duan Heng was made Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Rong, Hanlin academician, was appointed vice director of the Secretariat and concurrent grand chancellor; Duan Heng, inner reception commissioner, became commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 宰相屢請立皇子為王，上曰：「諸子皆幼，且功臣之子皆未加恩，而獨先朕子，皆自安乎！」

translations.literal: The chief ministers repeatedly asked to enfeoff the princes as kings. The Emperor said: "All my sons are still young, and the sons of meritorious officials have not yet been favored—if I alone advance my sons first, will they all feel secure!"
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers repeatedly urged enfeoffing the imperial princes as kings. Later Zhou Emperor Shizong said, "My sons are all still young, and the sons of my meritorious officials have not yet been rewarded. If I favor my sons alone, will the others feel secure?"

sentences.zh: 周兵圍壽春，連年未下，城中食盡。

translations.literal: Zhou troops besieged Shouchun for years without taking it; food in the city was exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou forces had besieged Shouchun for years without capturing it; provisions inside the city were gone.

sentences.zh: 齊王景達自濠州遣應援使、永安節度使許文稹、都軍使邊鎬、北面招討使朱元將兵數萬，溯淮救之，軍於紫金山，列十餘寨如連珠，與城中烽火晨夕相應，又築甬道抵壽春，欲運糧以饋之，綿亙數十里。

translations.literal: Prince of Qi Jing Da from Haozhou sent Relief Commissioner Xu Wenzhen, military governor of Yong'an, Chief Army Commander Bian Hao, and Northern Campaign Commissioner Zhu Yuan with tens of thousands of troops upstream on the Huai to save the city. They encamped at Purple Gold Mountain, arraying more than ten camps like linked pearls, coordinating beacon fires with the city morning and evening. They also built a covered road reaching Shouchun, intending to transport grain to supply it, stretching continuously for several tens of li.
translations.idiomatic: From Haozhou, Prince of Qi Jing Da dispatched Relief Commissioner Xu Wenzhen, military governor of Yong'an, Chief Army Commander Bian Hao, and Northern Campaign Commissioner Zhu Yuan with tens of thousands of men up the Huai to relieve the city. They camped on Purple Gold Mountain in more than ten linked fortifications, exchanging beacon signals with Shouchun day and night. They also built a covered supply route into the city, stretching for dozens of li to bring in grain.

sentences.zh: 將及壽春，李重進邀擊，大破之，死者五千人，奪其二寨。

translations.literal: As they were nearing Shouchun, Li Chongjin intercepted and attacked, inflicting a great defeat; five thousand died and two of their camps were taken.
translations.idiomatic: As they approached Shouchun, Li Chongjin intercepted them and won a crushing victory: five thousand were killed and two camps captured.

sentences.zh: 丁未，重進以聞。

translations.literal: On dingwei, Chongjin reported this.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingwei day, Li Chongjin reported the victory.

sentences.zh: 戊申，詔以來月幸淮上。

translations.literal: On wushen, an edict ordered that the following month the Emperor would travel to the Huai region.
translations.idiomatic: On the wushen day, an edict announced that the Emperor would visit the Huai front the following month.

sentences.zh: 劉仁贍請以邊鎬守城，自帥眾決戰，齊王景達不許，仁贍憤邑成疾。

translations.literal: Liu Renshan asked that Bian Hao hold the city while he himself led the army in a decisive battle; Prince of Qi Jing Da did not permit it, and Renshan, resentful and distressed, fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Renshan asked to leave Bian Hao to hold the city while he led the main force into decisive battle; Prince of Qi Jing Da refused, and Renshan, bitter and aggrieved, fell ill.

sentences.zh: 其幼子崇諫夜泛舟渡淮北，為小校所執，仁贍命腰斬之，左右莫敢救，監軍使周廷構哭於中門以救之，仁贍不許。

translations.literal: His youngest son Chongjian by night floated a boat across the Huai to the north bank and was seized by a junior officer. Renshan ordered him cut in two at the waist; those at his side dared not save him. Supervisory commissioner Zhou Tinggou wept at the middle gate to save him; Renshan would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son Chongjian rowed across the Huai by night to the north bank and was caught by a junior officer. Liu Renshan ordered him cut in two at the waist; no one at his side dared intervene. Supervisory commissioner Zhou Tinggou wept at the middle gate to plead for the boy, but Renshan refused.

sentences.zh: 廷構復使求救於夫人，夫人曰：「妾於崇諫非不愛也，然軍法不可私，名節不可虧，若貸之，則劉氏為不忠之門，妾與公何面目見將士乎！」

translations.literal: Tinggou again had someone plead with the lady. The lady said: "I am not without love for Chongjian, yet military law cannot be bent for private feeling, and one's reputation cannot be stained. If he were spared, the Liu house would become a house of disloyalty—what face would I and my lord have before the officers and men!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Tinggou appealed again to Lady Liu. She said, "I do love Chongjian, but military law admits no favoritism and honor cannot be compromised. If we spared him, the Liu name would stand for disloyalty—how could my husband and I face the troops?"

sentences.zh: 趣命斬之，然後成喪。

translations.literal: She urgently ordered him executed, and only then were funeral rites completed.
translations.idiomatic: She ordered the execution at once; only afterward were the funeral rites performed.

sentences.zh: 將士皆感泣。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers were all moved to tears.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and soldiers wept.

sentences.zh: 議者以唐援兵尚強，多請罷兵，帝疑之。

translations.literal: Advisers, because Tang relief troops were still strong, mostly asked to withdraw the army; the Emperor was doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: Many advisers, noting that Tang relief forces remained formidable, urged ending the campaign; Later Zhou Emperor Shizong hesitated.

sentences.zh: 李穀寢疾在第。

translations.literal: Li Gu was bedridden with illness at his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gu lay ill at home.

sentences.zh: 二月，丙寅，帝使范質、王溥就與之謀，穀上疏，以為：「壽春危困，破在旦夕，若鑾駕親征，則將士爭奮，援兵震恐，城中知亡，必可下矣！」

translations.literal: In the second month, on bingyin, the Emperor sent Fan Zhi and Wang Pu to consult with him. Gu submitted a memorial stating: "Shouchun is in peril and collapse is imminent. If the imperial carriage personally campaigns, officers and soldiers will strive to excel, relief troops will be terrified, and the city, knowing it is doomed, can certainly be taken!"
translations.idiomatic: “In the second month, on the bingyin day, the Emperor sent Fan Zhi and Wang Pu to consult Li Gu. Gu submitted a memorial arguing that Shouchun was near collapse, that an imperial expedition would galvanize Zhou troops and terrify the relief army, and that the city, seeing its end, would surely fall.”

sentences.zh: 上悅。

translations.literal: The Emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 庚午，詔有司更造祭器、祭玉等，命國子博士聶崇義討論制度，為之圖。

translations.literal: On gengwu, an edict ordered the relevant offices to remake sacrificial vessels, jade, and the like, and appointed National University Erudite Nie Chongyi to discuss the regulations and draw diagrams.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengwu day, an edict ordered new sacrificial vessels and ritual jades to be made and appointed Nie Chongyi, erudite of the National University, to study the regulations and draft diagrams.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，以王朴權東京留守兼判開封府事，以三司使張美為大內都巡檢，以侍衛都虞候韓通為京城內外都巡檢。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, Wang Pu was made acting Eastern Capital garrison commander and concurrent administrator of Kaifeng; Zhang Mei, commissioner of the Three Departments, was made chief inspector of the Inner Palace; Han Tong, chief adjutant of the Imperial Guard, was made chief inspector inside and outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiaxu day, Wang Pu was made acting Eastern Capital garrison commander and concurrent administrator of Kaifeng; Zhang Mei, commissioner of the Three Departments, became chief inspector of the Inner Palace; and Han Tong, chief adjutant of the Imperial Guard, became chief inspector of the capital inside and out.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，帝發大梁。

translations.literal: On yihai, the Emperor departed from Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: On the yihai day, Later Zhou Emperor Shizong set out from Daliang.

sentences.zh: 先是周與唐戰，唐水軍銳敏，周人無以敵之，帝每以為恨。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhou and Tang fought, Tang naval forces were sharp and agile and Zhou men had no way to match them; the Emperor always regretted this.
translations.idiomatic: In earlier Zhou-Tang fighting, Tang warships had been swift and skilled while Zhou forces had no answer for them—a source of constant regret to the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 返自壽春，於大梁城西汴水側造戰艦數百艘，命唐降卒教北人水戰，數月之後，縱橫出沒，殆勝唐兵。

translations.literal: Returning from Shouchun, on the west side of the Bian River outside Daliang he built several hundred warships and ordered Tang surrendered soldiers to teach northerners naval warfare. After several months they moved freely on the water and nearly surpassed Tang troops.
translations.idiomatic: After returning from Shouchun he built several hundred warships on the Bian west of Daliang and had Tang prisoners teach northern troops river fighting. Within months they maneuvered freely on the water and were nearly the equal of Tang sailors.

sentences.zh: 至是命右驍衛大將軍王環將水軍數千自閔河沿穎入淮，唐人見之大驚。

translations.literal: At this time he ordered Right Brave Guard General Wang Huan to lead several thousand naval troops from the Min River along the Ying into the Huai; Tang men were greatly alarmed when they saw them.
translations.idiomatic: Now he ordered Wang Huan, general of the Right Brave Guard, to lead several thousand sailors from the Min River along the Ying into the Huai; the Tang forces were stunned.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，帝至下蔡。

translations.literal: On yiyou, the Emperor reached Xiaqi.
translations.idiomatic: On the yiyou day, the Emperor arrived at Xiaqi.

sentences.zh: 三月，己丑夜，帝渡淮，抵壽春城下。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the night of jichou, the Emperor crossed the Huai and reached beneath the walls of Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the night of jichou, the Emperor crossed the Huai and came beneath the walls of Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 庚寅旦，躬擐甲冑，軍於紫金山南，命太祖皇帝擊唐先鋒寨及山北一寨，皆破之，斬獲三千餘級，斷其甬道，由是唐兵首尾不能相救。

translations.literal: At dawn on gengyin he personally donned armor, encamped south of Purple Gold Mountain, and ordered Zhao Kuangyin to attack the Tang vanguard camp and one camp north of the mountain; both were broken, more than three thousand were killed or captured, and the covered road was severed—thus Tang troops at either end could not rescue each other.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on gengyin he donned armor himself and encamped south of Purple Gold Mountain. He ordered Zhao Kuangyin to strike the Tang vanguard camp and a northern camp; both fell, with more than three thousand killed or captured, and the supply route was cut so Tang forces at either end could not aid each other.

sentences.zh: 至暮，帝分兵守諸寨，還下蔡。

translations.literal: At dusk the Emperor divided troops to hold the various camps and returned to Xiaqi.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk he left detachments to hold the camps and returned to Xiaqi.

sentences.zh: 唐朱元恃功，頗違元帥節度；

translations.literal: Zhu Yuan of Tang, relying on his achievements, frequently disobeyed the commander-in-chief's orders;
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yuan of Tang, proud of his record, often defied the commander-in-chief;

sentences.zh: 陳覺與元有隙，屢表元反覆，不可將兵，唐主以武昌節度使楊守忠代之。

translations.literal: Chen Jue had a grudge against Yuan and repeatedly memorialized that Yuan was fickle and unfit to command troops; the Southern Tang ruler replaced him with Yang Shouzhong, military governor of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jue bore a grudge against Zhu Yuan and repeatedly reported that Yuan was unreliable and unfit to command; the Southern Tang ruler replaced him with Yang Shouzhong, military governor of Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 守忠至濠州，覺以齊王景達之命，召元至濠州計事，將奪其兵。

translations.literal: When Shouzhong reached Haozhou, Jue, in Prince of Qi Jing Da's name, summoned Yuan to Haozhou to discuss affairs, intending to strip him of his command.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Shouzhong reached Haozhou, Chen Jue, invoking Prince of Qi Jing Da's authority, summoned Zhu Yuan to Haozhou on pretext of consultation, intending to seize his army.

sentences.zh: 元聞之，憤怒，欲自殺，門下客宋□說元曰：「大丈夫何往不富貴，何必為妻子死乎！」

translations.literal: When Yuan heard of it he was furious and wished to kill himself. His client Song Qi persuaded Yuan, saying: "A great man can find wealth and honor wherever he goes—why die for wife and children!"
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Yuan learned of this he was enraged and ready to take his own life. His adviser Song Qi urged him, "A true man can win wealth and rank wherever he turns—why die for your family?"

sentences.zh: 辛卯夜，元與先鋒壕寨使朱仁裕等舉寨萬餘人降，裨將時厚卿不從，元殺之。

translations.literal: On the night of xinmao, Yuan with Vanguard Trench Camp Commissioner Zhu Renyu and others led more than ten thousand men in their camp to surrender; deputy general Shi Houqing would not follow, and Yuan killed him.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of xinmao, Zhu Yuan with Zhu Renyu, commissioner of the vanguard trench camp, and others surrendered their camp of more than ten thousand men; deputy commander Shi Houqing refused, and Yuan killed him.

sentences.zh: 帝慮其餘眾沿流東潰，遽命虎捷左廂都指揮使趙晁將水軍數千沿淮而下。

translations.literal: The Emperor feared the remaining masses would flee east along the river; he urgently ordered Zhao Chao, commander of the Left Wing of the Tiger Vanguard, to lead several thousand naval troops downstream along the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the remaining Tang troops would flee east along the river, the Emperor immediately ordered Zhao Chao, commander of the Left Wing of the Tiger Vanguard, to lead several thousand sailors down the Huai.

sentences.zh: 壬辰旦，帝軍於趙步，諸將擊唐紫金山寨，大破之，殺獲萬餘人，擒許文稹、邊鎬、楊守忠。

translations.literal: At dawn on renchen the Emperor encamped at Zhaobu; the generals attacked the Tang camps on Purple Gold Mountain, inflicting a great defeat, killing and capturing more than ten thousand, and capturing Xu Wenzhen, Bian Hao, and Yang Shouzhong.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on renchen the Emperor encamped at Zhaobu. His generals stormed the Tang camps on Purple Gold Mountain, killing and capturing more than ten thousand men and taking Xu Wenzhen, Bian Hao, and Yang Shouzhong.

sentences.zh: 餘眾果沿淮東走，帝自趙步將騎數百循北岸追之，諸將以步騎循南岸追之，水軍自中流而下，唐兵戰溺死及降者殆四萬人，獲船艦糧仗以十萬數。

translations.literal: The remaining masses indeed fled east along the Huai. The Emperor from Zhaobu led several hundred cavalry along the north bank in pursuit; the generals pursued with infantry and cavalry along the south bank; the navy came down the middle of the stream. Tang troops killed, drowned, or surrendered numbered nearly forty thousand; ships, grain, and weapons captured numbered in the hundreds of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The survivors fled east along the Huai as expected. From Zhaobu the Emperor led several hundred horsemen along the north bank; generals pursued on the south bank with infantry and cavalry while the fleet closed from midstream. Nearly forty thousand Tang soldiers were killed, drowned, or captured; booty in ships, grain, and arms ran into the hundreds of thousands.

sentences.zh: 晡時，帝馳至荊山洪，距趙步二百餘里。

translations.literal: In the late afternoon the Emperor galloped to Jingshan Hong, more than two hundred li from Zhaobu.
translations.idiomatic: By late afternoon the Emperor had galloped to Jingshan Hong, more than two hundred li from Zhaobu.

sentences.zh: 是夜，宿鎮淮軍，癸酉，從官始至。

translations.literal: That night he lodged at Zhenhuai Army. On guiyou the attendants first arrived.
translations.idiomatic: That night he lodged at Zhenhuai Army; on the guiyou day his attendants finally caught up.

sentences.zh: 劉仁贍聞援兵敗，扼吭歎息。

translations.literal: When Liu Renshan heard the relief army had been defeated, he clutched his throat and sighed.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Renshan heard that the relief army had been destroyed, he clutched his throat and groaned.

sentences.zh: 甲午，發近縣丁夫數千城鎮淮軍，為二城，夾淮水，徙下蔡浮梁於其間，扼濠、壽應援之路。

translations.literal: On jiawu, several thousand corvée laborers from nearby counties were mobilized to fortify Zhenhuai Army into two cities flanking the Huai; the Xiaqi pontoon bridge was moved between them, blocking the relief routes from Hao and Shou.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiawu day, several thousand laborers from nearby counties were mobilized to fortify Zhenhuai Army as twin cities on either side of the Huai; the Xiaqi pontoon bridge was shifted between them to choke off relief from Hao and Shou.

sentences.zh: 會淮水漲，唐濠州都監彭城郭廷謂以水軍溯淮，欲掩不備，焚浮梁。

translations.literal: When the Huai rose, Guo Tingwei, Tang garrison commander of Hao prefecture from Pengcheng, intended to lead naval troops upstream on the Huai, catch the Zhou unprepared, and burn the pontoon bridge.
translations.idiomatic: When the Huai flooded, Guo Tingwei, Tang garrison commander of Hao from Pengcheng, planned to lead warships upstream, strike by surprise, and burn the pontoon bridge.

sentences.zh: 右龍武統軍趙匡贊覘知之，伏兵邀擊，破之。

translations.literal: Zhao Kuangzan, commanding general of the Right Dragon Martial Guard, detected this and with hidden troops intercepted and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Kuangzan, commanding general of the Right Dragon Martial Guard, learned of the plan and ambushed him, winning a victory.

sentences.zh: 唐齊王景達及陳覺皆自濠州奔歸金陵，惟靜江指揮使陳德誠全軍而還。

translations.literal: Prince of Qi Jing Da of Tang and Chen Jue both fled from Haozhou back to Jinling; only Chen Decheng, commander of the Jingjiang Guard, returned with his army intact.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qi Jing Da and Chen Jue both fled from Haozhou to Jinling; only Chen Decheng, commander of the Jingjiang Guard, brought his force back intact.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，以淮南節度使向訓為武寧節度使、淮南道行營都監，將兵戍鎮淮軍。

translations.literal: On wuxu, Xiang Xun, military governor of Huainan, was made military governor of Wuning and overall supervisor of the Huainan campaign, leading troops to garrison Zhenhuai Army.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuxu day, Xiang Xun, military governor of Huainan, was appointed military governor of Wuning and overall supervisor of the Huainan campaign, with orders to garrison Zhenhuai Army.

sentences.zh: 己亥，上自鎮淮軍復如下蔡。

translations.literal: On jihai the Emperor returned from Zhenhuai Army to Xiaqi again.
translations.idiomatic: On the jihai day, Later Zhou Emperor Shizong returned from Zhenhuai Army to Xiaqi.

sentences.zh: 庚子，賜劉仁贍詔，使自擇禍福。

translations.literal: On gengzi he granted Liu Renshan an edict, letting him choose fortune or calamity for himself.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengzi day he sent Liu Renshan an edict offering him the choice of surrender or ruin.

sentences.zh: 唐主議自督諸將拒周，中書舍人喬匡舜上疏切諫，唐主以為沮眾，流撫州。

translations.literal: The Southern Tang ruler planned to personally supervise the generals in resisting Zhou. Secretariat drafter Qiao Kuangshun submitted a forceful memorial of remonstrance; the Southern Tang ruler considered this discouraging to the troops and exiled him to Fu prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Tang ruler planned to take the field himself against Zhou. Qiao Kuangshun, a secretariat drafter, submitted a blunt memorial of protest; the ruler judged it demoralizing and banished him to Fu prefecture.

sentences.zh: 唐主問神衛統軍朱匡業、劉存忠以守禦方略，匡業誦羅隱詩曰：「時來天地皆同力，運去英雄不自由。」

translations.literal: The Southern Tang ruler asked Divine Guard commanding generals Zhu Kuangye and Liu Cunzhong for defensive strategy. Kuangye recited a poem by Luo Yin, saying: "When the time comes, heaven and earth all lend their strength; when fortune departs, even heroes are not their own masters."
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Tang ruler asked Zhu Kuangye and Liu Cunzhong, commanding generals of the Divine Guard, for a defense plan. Zhu Kuangye quoted Luo Yin: "When fortune turns, heaven and earth all lend their strength; when it turns away, even heroes are not their own masters."

sentences.zh: 存忠以匡業言為然。

translations.literal: Cunzhong considered Kuangye's words correct.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cunzhong agreed with Zhu Kuangye's view.

sentences.zh: 唐主怒，貶匡業撫州副使，流存忠於饒州。

translations.literal: The Southern Tang ruler was angry, demoted Kuangye to deputy commissioner of Fu prefecture, and exiled Cunzhong to Rao prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Tang ruler was furious: Zhu Kuangye was demoted to deputy commissioner of Fu prefecture and Liu Cunzhong was exiled to Rao prefecture.

sentences.zh: 既而竟不敢自出。

translations.literal: In the end he still did not dare go out himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he still did not dare take the field in person.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，帝耀兵於壽春城北。

translations.literal: On jiachen, the Emperor displayed his troops north of Shouchun city.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiachen day, Later Zhou Emperor Shizong reviewed his army north of Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 唐清淮節度使兼侍中劉仁贍病甚，不知人，丙午，監軍使周廷構、營田副使孫羽等作仁贍表，遣使奉之來降。

translations.literal: Liu Renshan, Tang military governor of Qinghuai and concurrent palace attendant, was gravely ill and unconscious. On bingwu, supervisory commissioner Zhou Tinggou, deputy commissioner of garrison farms Sun Yu, and others drafted a memorial for Renshan and sent envoys presenting it to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Renshan, Southern Tang military governor of Qinghuai and palace attendant, lay gravely ill and insensible. On the bingwu day, supervisory commissioner Zhou Tinggou, garrison-farm deputy Sun Yu, and others drafted a surrender memorial in his name and sent envoys with it.

sentences.zh: 丁未，帝賜仁贍詔，遣闔門使萬年張保續入城宣諭，仁贍子崇讓復出謝罪。

translations.literal: On dingwei, the Emperor granted Renshan an edict and sent Zhang Baoxu of Wannian, commissioner of the Gate, into the city to proclaim it. Renshan's son Chongrang again came out to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingwei day the Emperor issued an edict to Liu Renshan and sent Zhang Baoxu of Wannian, commissioner of the Gate, into the city to announce it. Liu Renshan's son Chongrang came out again to submit.

sentences.zh: 戊申，帝大陳甲兵，受降於壽春城北，廷構等舁仁贍出城，仁贍臥不能起，帝慰勞賜賚，復令入城養疾。

translations.literal: On wushen, the Emperor greatly arrayed armored troops and accepted the surrender north of Shouchun city. Tinggou and the others carried Renshan out of the city; Renshan lay unable to rise. The Emperor consoled and rewarded him, then ordered him back into the city to recover from illness.
translations.idiomatic: On the wushen day the Emperor paraded his armored host and accepted the surrender north of Shouchun. Zhou Tinggou and the others carried Liu Renshan out; he could not rise from his couch. The Emperor comforted and rewarded him, then sent him back into the city to convalesce.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，徙壽州治下蔡，赦州境死罪以下。

translations.literal: On gengxu, the seat of Shou prefecture was moved to Xiaqi, and crimes below capital punishment within the prefecture were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengxu day the administrative seat of Shou prefecture was moved to Xiaqi, and all crimes short of capital punishment in the prefecture were pardoned.

sentences.zh: 州民受唐文書聚山林者，並召令復業，勿問罪。

translations.literal: Commoners in the prefecture who had received Tang documents and gathered in the mountains were all summoned to resume their livelihoods without inquiry into their offenses.
translations.idiomatic: People who had taken Tang commissions and fled to the hills were summoned home without punishment.

sentences.zh: 有嘗為其殺傷者，毋得仇訟。

translations.literal: Those who had once been killed or wounded by them were not permitted to seek revenge in lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had suffered injury at their hands were forbidden to sue for revenge.

sentences.zh: 曏日政令有不便於民者，令本州條奏。

translations.literal: Where past government orders had been inconvenient for the people, the prefecture was ordered to list and report them.
translations.idiomatic: Any past policies that had burdened the people were to be listed and reported by the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，以劉仁贍為天平節度使兼中書令，制辭略曰：「盡忠所事，抗節無虧，前代名臣，幾人堪比！

translations.literal: On xinhai, Liu Renshan was made military governor of Tianping and concurrent Grand Chancellor. The edict of appointment stated in part: "Serving one's lord with full loyalty and unblemished integrity—how many famed ministers of former ages could compare!
translations.idiomatic: On the xinhai day Liu Renshan was appointed military governor of Tianping and concurrent grand chancellor. The appointment edict read in part, "Loyal in service and unyielding in integrity—how few ministers of old could match you!

sentences.zh: 朕之伐叛，得爾為多。」

translations.literal: In my campaign against rebellion, gaining you counts for much."
translations.idiomatic: In this campaign against rebellion, winning you over means more than any victory."

sentences.zh: 是日，卒，追賜爵彭城郡主。

translations.literal: That same day he died; posthumously he was enfeoffed as Duke of Pengcheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He died the same day and was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Pengcheng commandery.

sentences.zh: 唐主聞之，亦贈太師。

translations.literal: When the Southern Tang ruler heard of it, he also posthumously awarded him Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Southern Tang ruler learned of his death, he too posthumously made Liu Renshan grand preceptor.

sentences.zh: 帝復以清淮軍為忠正軍，以旌仁贍之節，以右羽林統軍楊信為忠正節度使、同平章事。

translations.literal: The Emperor again renamed the Qinghuai Army the Zhongzheng Army to honor Renshan's integrity, and made Yang Xin, commanding general of the Right Forest Guard, military governor of Zhongzheng and concurrent Grand Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor renamed the Qinghuai Army the Loyalty Army to honor Liu Renshan's integrity and appointed Yang Xin, commanding general of the Right Forest Guard, as its military governor and concurrent grand chancellor.

sentences.zh: 前許州司馬韓倫，侍衛馬軍都指揮使令坤之父也。

translations.literal: Former defender marshal of Xu prefecture Han Lun was the father of Ling Kun, commander of the Palace Cavalry of the Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Han Lun, former defender marshal of Xu prefecture, was the father of Ling Kun, commander of the Palace Cavalry of the Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 令坤領鎮安節度使，倫居於陳州，干預政事，貪污不法，為公私患，為人所訟，令坤屢為之泣請。

translations.literal: Ling Kun held the post of military governor of Zhen'an; Lun lived at Chen prefecture, meddled in government affairs, was corrupt and lawless, became a public and private nuisance, and was sued by others. Ling Kun repeatedly wept and pleaded on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Ling Kun served as military governor of Zhen'an while Han Lun lived at Chen prefecture, meddling in affairs, taking bribes, and breaking the law until he became a plague to officials and commoners alike. When suits were brought against him, Ling Kun wept and pleaded repeatedly for mercy.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，詔免倫死，流沙門島。

translations.literal: On guichou, an edict spared Lun death and exiled him to Shamen Island.
translations.idiomatic: On the guichou day an edict spared Han Lun's life and exiled him to Shamen Island.

sentences.zh: 倫後得赦還，居洛陽，與光祿卿致仕柴守禮及當時將相王溥、王晏、王彥超之父游處，恃勢恣橫，洛陽人畏之，謂之十阿父。

translations.literal: Lun was later pardoned and returned, living at Luoyang. He associated with Chai Shouli, retired director of the Court of Imperial Regalia, and the fathers of the then generals and chancellors Wang Pu, Wang Yan, and Wang Yanchao, relying on their power and acting arrogantly. The people of Luoyang feared them and called them the Ten Honored Fathers.
translations.idiomatic: Later pardoned, Han Lun returned to Luoyang and kept company with the retired director of the Court of Imperial Regalia Chai Shouli and the fathers of leading ministers and generals such as Wang Pu, Wang Yan, and Wang Yanchao. They threw their weight around, and Luoyang feared them as the Ten Honored Fathers.

sentences.zh: 帝既為太祖嗣，人無敢言守禮子者，但以元舅處之，優其俸給，未嘗至大梁。

translations.literal: Since the Emperor had succeeded as heir to the Founding Emperor, no one dared speak of Shouli as the Emperor's son; he was treated only as the maternal uncle, given generous stipends, and never came to Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: Because Later Zhou Emperor Shizong had succeeded as heir to the founding emperor, no one dared say openly that Chai Shouli was the Emperor's father; he was treated as the maternal uncle, given generous stipends, and never came to Daliang.

sentences.zh: 嘗以小忿殺人，有司不敢詰，帝知而不問。

translations.literal: He once killed a man in a minor quarrel; the officials dared not investigate, and the Emperor knew but did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Once, over a petty quarrel, he killed a man; officials dared not investigate, and the Emperor, knowing, let the matter pass.

sentences.zh: 詔開壽州倉振饑民。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Shou prefecture granary opened to relieve the hungry people.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Shou prefecture's granaries opened to feed the starving.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，帝北還，夏，四月，己巳，至大梁。

translations.literal: On bingchen the Emperor returned north. In summer, the fourth month, on jisi, he reached Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingchen day the Emperor marched north. In summer, the fourth month, on the jisi day, he reached Daliang.

sentences.zh: 詔修永福殿，命宦官孫延希董其役。

translations.literal: An edict ordered repairs to Yongfu Hall and appointed the eunuch Sun Yanxi to supervise the work.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the repair of Yongfu Hall and put the eunuch Sun Yanxi in charge of the project.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，帝至其所，見役徒有削柿為匕，瓦中啖飯者，大怒，斬延希於市。

translations.literal: On dingchou the Emperor went to the site and saw laborers carving persimmons into spoons and eating rice from tile bowls. He was greatly angered and executed Yanxi in the market.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingchou day the Emperor inspected the site and found laborers carving persimmons into spoons and eating from tile bowls. Enraged, he had Sun Yanxi executed in the market.

sentences.zh: 帝之克秦、鳳也，以蜀兵數千人為懷恩軍。

translations.literal: When the Emperor conquered Qin and Feng, he enrolled several thousand Shu soldiers as the Huai'en Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Later Zhou Emperor Shizong conquered Qin and Feng, he enrolled several thousand Shu prisoners in the Gratitude Army.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，遣懷恩指揮使蕭知遠等將士八百餘人西還。

translations.literal: On yihai he sent Huai'en Army commander Xiao Zhiyuan and more than eight hundred officers and soldiers back west.
translations.idiomatic: On the yihai day he sent Xiao Zhiyuan, commander of the Gratitude Army, and more than eight hundred men back west.

sentences.zh: 壬午，李穀扶疾入見，帝命不拜，坐於御坐之側。

translations.literal: On renwu, Li Gu, supporting himself through illness, came to audience. The Emperor ordered that he need not bow and had him sit beside the imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: On the renwu day Li Gu came to audience despite his illness. The Emperor exempted him from bowing and seated him beside the throne.

sentences.zh: 穀懇辭祿位，不許。

translations.literal: Gu earnestly declined salary and office; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gu earnestly asked to resign his salary and office; the Emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 甲申，分江南降卒為六軍、三十指揮，號懷德軍。

translations.literal: On jiashen, surrendered soldiers from Jiangnan were divided into six armies and thirty commands, called the Huaide Army.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiashen day surrendered troops from Jiangnan were organized into six armies and thirty commands as the Virtue Army.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，詔疏汴水北入五丈河，由是齊、魯舟楫皆達於大梁。

translations.literal: On yiyou, an edict ordered the Bian River dredged northward into the Wuzhang River, whereby boats from Qi and Lu all reached Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: On the yiyou day an edict ordered the Bian River dredged north into the Wuzhang River so that shipping from Qi and Lu could reach Daliang.

sentences.zh: 五月，丁酉，以太祖皇帝領義成節度使。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on dingyou, Zhao Kuangyin was made acting military governor of Yicheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the dingyou day, Zhao Kuangyin was appointed acting military governor of Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 詔以律令文古難知，格敕煩雜不壹，命侍御史知雜事張湜等訓釋，詳定為《刑統》。

translations.literal: An edict stated that the statutes were ancient and hard to understand and the supplementary edicts numerous and inconsistent, and ordered Supervising Censor Zhang Si and others to annotate and compile them definitively as the Penal Code Compendium.
translations.idiomatic: An edict noted that the statutes were archaic and obscure and the supplementary edicts numerous and inconsistent, and ordered Supervising Censor Zhang Si and others to annotate and compile them into the Penal Code Compendium.

sentences.zh: 唐郭遷謂將水軍斷渦口浮梁，又襲敗武寧節度使武行德於定遠，行德僅以身免。

translations.literal: Guo Tingwei of Tang intended to lead naval troops to cut the pontoon bridge at Wokou and also launched a surprise attack defeating Wu Xingde, military governor of Wuning, at Dingyuan; Xingde barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Tingwei of Tang planned to sever the pontoon bridge at Wokou with warships and also surprised Wu Xingde, military governor of Wuning, at Dingyuan; Wu Xingde barely escaped alive.

sentences.zh: 唐主以廷謂為滁州團練使，充上淮水陸應援使。

translations.literal: The Southern Tang ruler made Tingwei regimental commander of Chu prefecture and overall land-and-water relief commissioner for upper Huai.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Tang ruler made Guo Tingwei regimental commander of Chu prefecture and overall land-and-water relief commissioner for the upper Huai.

sentences.zh: 蜀人多言左右衛聖馬步都指揮使、保寧節度使、同平章事李廷珪為將敗覆，不應復典兵，廷珪亦自請罷去。

translations.literal: Many in Shu said that Li Tinggui, Left and Right Guard commanding general of horse and foot, military governor of Baoning, and concurrent Grand Chancellor, had failed as a general and should not again command troops; Tinggui also asked to be relieved.
translations.idiomatic: Many in Shu argued that Li Tinggui—commanding general of the Left and Right Guard, military governor of Baoning, and concurrent grand chancellor—had failed in command and should not lead troops again; Tinggui himself asked to step down.

sentences.zh: 六月，乙丑，蜀主加廷珪檢校太尉，罷軍職。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on chou, the Shu ruler added Tinggui as Grand Preceptor with inspection and removed him from military office.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the chou day, the Shu ruler promoted Li Tinggui to inspected grand preceptor and relieved him of military command.

sentences.zh: 李太后以典兵者多非其人，謂蜀主曰：「吾昔見莊宗跨河與梁戰，及先帝在太原，平二蜀，諸將非有大功，無得典兵，故士卒畏服。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Li, because many who held military command were unfit for the role, told the Shu ruler: "I once saw Emperor Zhuangzong cross the river to fight Liang, and when the late emperor was at Taiyuan and pacified the two Shu regions, generals without great merit were not allowed to command troops—therefore the soldiers feared and obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Li, believing many current commanders were unfit, told the Shu ruler, "I saw Emperor Zhuangzong cross the Yellow River to fight Liang, and when our late emperor was at Taiyuan and pacified the two Shu regions, only generals of real merit were allowed to command—so the troops obeyed.

sentences.zh: 今王昭遠出於廝養，伊審徵、韓保貞、趙崇韜皆膏粱乳臭子，素不習兵，徒以舊恩置於人上，平時誰敢言者！

translations.literal: Now Wang Zhaoyuan rose from stable service; Yi Shenzheng, Han Baozhen, and Zhao Chongtao are all pampered sons of rich families who have never studied warfare, yet were placed above others solely through old favor—who dared speak in normal times!
translations.idiomatic: Now Wang Zhaoyuan came up from the stables; Yi Shenzheng, Han Baozhen, and Zhao Chongtao are spoiled sons of the elite who never learned war, yet old favor put them in command—who dared object in peacetime?

sentences.zh: 一旦疆場有事，安能御大敵乎！

translations.literal: If the frontier suddenly has trouble, how can they withstand a great enemy!
translations.idiomatic: When the border flares up, how will they face a serious enemy?

sentences.zh: 以吾觀之，惟高彥儔太原舊人，終不負汝，自餘無足任者。」

translations.literal: In my view, only Gao Yanzhou, an old follower from Taiyuan, will never fail you; apart from him none are fit for the task."
translations.idiomatic: In my view only Gao Yanzhou, an old Taiyuan comrade, will not fail you; beyond him none are fit."

sentences.zh: 蜀主不能從。

translations.literal: The Shu ruler could not follow this advice.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu ruler would not heed her.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，以前華州刺史王祚為穎州團練使。

translations.literal: On dingchou, former governor of Hua prefecture Wang Zuo was made regimental commander of Ying prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingchou day, former governor of Hua prefecture Wang Zuo was appointed regimental commander of Ying prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祚，溥之父也。

translations.literal: Zuo was Pu's father.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zuo was Wang Pu's father.

sentences.zh: 溥為宰相，祚有賓客，溥常朝服侍立。

translations.literal: Pu was chief minister; when Zuo had guests, Pu would often attend court in formal dress and stand in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pu was chief minister; when Wang Zuo entertained guests, Pu would often attend in court dress and stand waiting on him.

sentences.zh: 客坐不安席，祚曰：「犬屯犬不足為起。」

translations.literal: The guest would be unable to sit at ease. Zuo said: "A dog attending a dog is not worth rising for."
translations.idiomatic: Guests could not sit comfortably. Wang Zuo said, "When a dog waits on a dog, one need not stand."

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丁亥，上治定遠軍及壽春城南之敗，以武寧節度使兼中書令武行德為左衛上將軍，河陽節度使李繼勳為右衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on dinghai, the Emperor dealt with the defeats at Dingyuan Army and south of Shouchun city, making Wu Xingde, military governor of Wuning and concurrent Grand Chancellor, General of the Left Guard, and Li Jixun, military governor of Heyang, General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on the dinghai day, Later Zhou Emperor Shizong punished the defeats at Dingyuan Army and south of Shouchun: Wu Xingde, military governor of Wuning and concurrent grand chancellor, was made general of the Left Guard, and Li Jixun, military governor of Heyang, general of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 北漢主初立七廟。

translations.literal: The Northern Han ruler for the first time established seven ancestral temples.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Han ruler established seven ancestral temples for the first time.

sentences.zh: 司空兼門下侍郎、同平章事李穀臥疾二年，凡九表辭位，八月，乙亥，罷守本官，令每月肩輿一詣便殿議政事。

translations.literal: Minister of Works and concurrent Vice Director of the Chancellery and Grand Chancellor Li Gu had been bedridden for two years and nine times submitted memorials resigning office. In the eighth month, on yihai, he was relieved of concurrent duties and retained his original office, ordered once each month to be carried in a sedan to the informal hall to discuss state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gu, minister of works, vice director of the Chancellery, and grand chancellor, had been bedridden for two years and nine times asked to resign. In the eighth month, on the yihai day, he was relieved of his concurrent posts but kept his base rank, with orders to be carried once a month to the informal hall to discuss policy.

sentences.zh: 以樞密副使、戶部侍郎王朴檢校太保，充樞密使。

translations.literal: Wang Pu, Deputy Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Vice Minister of Revenue, was made Grand Guardian with inspection and full Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pu, deputy commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and vice minister of revenue, was promoted to inspected grand guardian and full commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 懷恩軍至成都，蜀主遣梓州別駕胡立等八十人東還，且致書為謝，請通好。

translations.literal: When the Huai'en Army reached Chengdu, the Shu ruler sent Hu Li of Zizhou, deputy prefect, and eighty others back east, also sending a letter of thanks and requesting friendly relations.
translations.idiomatic: When the Gratitude Army reached Chengdu, the Shu ruler sent Hu Li, deputy prefect of Zizhou, and eighty others back east with a letter of thanks seeking friendly relations.

sentences.zh: 癸未，立等至大梁。

translations.literal: On guiwei, Li and the others reached Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiwei day, Hu Li's party reached Daliang.

sentences.zh: 帝以蜀主抗禮，不之答。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because the Shu ruler used equal ceremonial forms, did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhou Emperor Shizong, offended that the Shu ruler addressed him as an equal, made no reply.

sentences.zh: 蜀主聞之，怒曰：「朕為天子郊祀天地時，爾猶作賊，何敢如是！」

translations.literal: When the Shu ruler heard of this he angrily said: "When I as Son of Heaven performed suburban sacrifices to heaven and earth, you were still a bandit—how dare you act thus!"
translations.idiomatic: When the Shu ruler heard this he raged, "When I as Son of Heaven sacrificed to heaven and earth, you were still a rebel—how dare you treat me so!"

sentences.zh: 九月，中書舍人竇儼上疏請令有司討論古今禮儀，作《大周通禮》，考正鐘律，作《大周正樂》。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Secretariat drafter Dou Yan submitted a memorial asking the relevant offices to discuss ancient and modern ritual, compile the Comprehensive Rites of Great Zhou, examine and correct bell and pitch standards, and compose the Correct Music of Great Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Dou Yan, a secretariat drafter, memorialized asking officials to study ancient and modern ritual, compile the Comprehensive Rites of Great Zhou, revise pitch standards, and compose the Correct Music of Great Zhou.

sentences.zh: 又以：「為政之本，莫大擇人；

translations.literal: He also stated: "The root of governing lies in nothing greater than choosing men;
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote, "The foundation of government is choosing the right men;

sentences.zh: 擇人之重，莫先宰相。

translations.literal: and among the weight of choosing men, nothing comes before the chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: and among all appointments, none matters more than the chief minister.

sentences.zh: 自有唐之末，輕用名器，始為輔弼，即兼三公、僕射之官。

translations.literal: From the end of Tang onward, honorary titles were lightly bestowed; as soon as one became an assistant counselor, he concurrently held the offices of the Three Excellencies or Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: Since late Tang, honors have been handed out too freely: the moment a man becomes a counselor he also holds the Three Excellencies or grand mentor.

sentences.zh: 故其未得之也，則以趨競為心；

translations.literal: Therefore before obtaining office, their hearts were set on scrambling in competition;
translations.idiomatic: Before they win office their hearts are set on scheming and rivalry;

sentences.zh: 既得之也，則以容默為事。

translations.literal: once obtained, they made silence and compliance their business.
translations.idiomatic: once in office they make silence and compliance their trade.

sentences.zh: 但思解密勿之務，守崇重之官，逍遙林亭，保安宗族。

translations.literal: They think only of keeping secrets and avoiding trouble, holding lofty offices, roaming in groves and pavilions, and securing their clans.
translations.idiomatic: They think only of keeping secrets, avoiding trouble, holding lofty rank, idling in gardens, and protecting their families.

sentences.zh: 乞令即日宰相於南宮三品、兩省給、捨以上，各舉所知。

translations.literal: I beg that starting today chief ministers be ordered, from third rank in the Southern Palace and drafters and reviewers of the Two Departments upward, each to recommend men they know.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that from today every chief minister, and every official from third rank in the Southern Palace and drafters and reviewers of the Two Departments upward, recommend men they know.

sentences.zh: 若陛下素知其賢，自可登庸；

translations.literal: If Your Majesty already knows a man's worth, he may be promoted directly;
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty already knows a man is worthy, appoint him at once;

sentences.zh: 若其未也，且令以本官權知政事。

translations.literal: if not yet known, let him temporarily manage affairs in his current office.
translations.idiomatic: if not, let him temporarily handle affairs at his current rank.

sentences.zh: 期歲之間，察其職業，若果能堪稱，其官已高，則除平章事；

translations.literal: Within the span of a year, examine his performance; if he truly proves adequate and his rank is already high, appoint him Grand Chancellor;
translations.idiomatic: Within a year examine his performance; if he proves capable and his rank is already high, make him grand chancellor;

sentences.zh: 未高，則稍更遷官，權知如故。

translations.literal: if not yet high, gradually transfer his rank while he continues to manage affairs as before.
translations.idiomatic: if his rank is not yet high, promote him step by step while he continues in temporary charge.

sentences.zh: 若有不稱，則罷其政事，責其舉者。

translations.literal: If he proves unfit, remove him from affairs and hold his recommender accountable.
translations.idiomatic: If he fails, remove him and hold his recommender responsible.

sentences.zh: 又，班行之中，有員無職者太半，乞量其才器，授以外任，試之於事，還則以舊官登敘，考其治狀，能者進之，否者黜之。」

translations.literal: Moreover, more than half of those in the official ranks hold posts without duties. I beg that their talent be measured and they be given outside assignments, tested in action; on return let them be promoted according to their old rank, their governance examined—capable men advanced, unfit men dismissed."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, more than half the court roster hold titles without duties. Measure their talent, send them to outside posts, and test them in office; on return promote by their old rank and judge their record—the able advanced, the unfit dismissed."

sentences.zh: 又請：「令盜賊自相糾告，以其所告貲產之半賞之；

translations.literal: He also requested: "Order bandits to inform on one another, rewarding the informer with half the reported property;
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed, "Let bandits inform on one another, rewarding the informer with half the reported property;

sentences.zh: 或親戚為之首，則論其徒侶而赦其所首者。

translations.literal: or if a kinsman turns others in first, punish the gang but pardon the one who informed.
translations.idiomatic: or if a kinsman turns in the rest first, punish the gang but pardon the informer.

sentences.zh: 如此，則盜不能聚矣。

translations.literal: In this way bandits cannot gather.
translations.idiomatic: That way bandits cannot gather in numbers.

sentences.zh: 又，新鄭鄉村團為義營，各立將佐，一戶為盜，累其一村；

translations.literal: Moreover, in Xinzheng village districts they formed righteous camps, each establishing commanders and deputies: if one household turned bandit, the whole village was implicated;
translations.idiomatic: In Xinzheng, village districts formed righteous camps with appointed leaders: if one household turned bandit, the whole village was implicated;

sentences.zh: 一戶被盜，罪其一將。

translations.literal: if one household was robbed, one commander was punished.
translations.idiomatic: if one household was robbed, its commander was punished.

sentences.zh: 每有盜發，則鳴鼓舉火，丁壯雲集，盜少民多，無能脫者。

translations.literal: Whenever bandits appeared, drums were beaten and fires raised; able-bodied men gathered like clouds. Bandits were few and the people many—none could escape.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits struck, drums sounded and fires were lit; able-bodied men gathered in clouds. Outnumbered, the thieves could not escape.

sentences.zh: 由是鄰縣充斥而一境獨清。

translations.literal: Thus neighboring counties were overrun while one district alone remained clear.
translations.idiomatic: Neighboring counties swarmed with thieves while that district alone stayed clear.

sentences.zh: 請令他縣皆效之，亦止盜之一術也。

translations.literal: I ask that other counties all imitate this—it is also one method for stopping bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Let other counties copy this—it is one way to stop banditry.

sentences.zh: 又，累朝已來，屢下詔書，聽民多種廣耕，止輸舊稅，及其既種，則有司履畝而增之，故民皆疑懼而田不加辟。

translations.literal: Moreover, for many reigns edicts have repeatedly allowed the people to plant widely and pay only the old tax; yet once they had planted, the offices measured acre by acre and increased the levy. Therefore the people are all suspicious and fearful and do not expand their fields.
translations.idiomatic: For reign after reign edicts have encouraged wider planting at the old tax rate, yet once fields were sown officials measured acre by acre and raised the levy. The people no longer trust the throne and will not open new land.

sentences.zh: 夫為政之先，莫如敦信，信苟著矣，則田無不廣，田廣則穀多，穀多則藏之民猶藏之官也。」

translations.literal: In governing, nothing comes before solid trust. If trust is established, no field will fail to be expanded; fields expanded, grain will be abundant; grain abundant, what the people store is as if stored by the state."
translations.idiomatic: Nothing in government comes before trust. Once trust is firm, fields will expand; expanded fields mean more grain; and grain in the people's bins is grain in the state's bins."

sentences.zh: 又言：「陛下南征江、淮，一舉而得八州，再駕而平壽春，威靈所加，前無強敵。

translations.literal: He also stated: "Your Majesty's southern expedition to the Jiang and Huai regions took eight prefectures in one stroke and pacified Shouchun on the second campaign; wherever your majesty and authority reached, no strong enemy stood before you.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote, "Your Majesty's southern campaign took eight prefectures at a stroke and Shouchun on the second advance; wherever your authority reached, no strong foe stood in the way.

sentences.zh: 今以眾擊寡，以治伐亂，勢無不克。

translations.literal: Now with many attacking few and order campaigning against chaos, there is no situation that cannot be conquered.
translations.idiomatic: Now, with numbers against weakness and order against chaos, nothing can stand before you.

sentences.zh: 但行之貴速，則彼民免俘馘之災，此民息轉輸之困矣。」

translations.literal: Only in execution speed is precious—then the people there will be spared the disaster of capture and slaughter, and the people here will be relieved of the hardship of transport."
translations.idiomatic: Only speed matters—then the enemy's people will be spared slaughter and our people spared the burden of supply."

sentences.zh: 帝覽而善之。

translations.literal: The Emperor read it and approved.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhou Emperor Shizong read the memorial and approved it.

sentences.zh: 儼，儀之弟也。

translations.literal: Yan was the younger brother of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Yan was the younger brother of Dou Yi.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，戊午，設賢良方正直言極諫、經學優深可為師法、詳閒吏理達於教化等科。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on wuwu, categories were established for worthy and upright men who speak bluntly and remonstrate, for those deeply versed in classical learning fit to serve as teachers, and for those well versed in administrative principles and skilled in moral transformation.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on the wuwu day, examination categories were established for worthy and upright remonstrators, for scholars fit to serve as teachers, and for men skilled in administration and moral transformation.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，北漢麟州刺史楊重訓舉城降，以為麟州防禦使。

translations.literal: On guihai, Yang Chongxun, governor of Lin prefecture in Northern Han, surrendered the city; he was made defender commissioner of Lin prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the guihai day, Yang Chongxun, governor of Lin prefecture in Northern Han, surrendered his city and was made defender commissioner of Lin.

sentences.zh: 己巳，以王朴為東京留守，聽以便宜從事。

translations.literal: On jisi, Wang Pu was made Eastern Capital garrison commander, authorized to act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: On the jisi day, Wang Pu was made Eastern Capital garrison commander with discretionary authority.

sentences.zh: 以三司使張美充大內都點檢。

translations.literal: Zhang Mei, commissioner of the Three Departments, was made chief inspector of the Inner Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mei, commissioner of the Three Departments, was appointed chief inspector of the Inner Palace.

sentences.zh: 壬申，帝發大梁；

translations.literal: On renshen, the Emperor departed from Daliang;
translations.idiomatic: On the renshen day, Later Zhou Emperor Shizong set out from Daliang;

sentences.zh: 十一月，丙戌，至鎮淮軍，是夜五鼓，濟淮；

translations.literal: in the eleventh month, on bingxu, he reached Zhenhuai Army. That night at the fifth watch he crossed the Huai;
translations.idiomatic: in the eleventh month, on the bingxu day, he reached Zhenhuai Army; that night at the fifth watch he crossed the Huai;

sentences.zh: 丁亥，至濠州城西。

translations.literal: on dinghai he reached west of Haozhou city.
translations.idiomatic: on the dinghai day he reached the west of Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 濠州東北十八里有灘，唐人柵於其上，環水自固，謂周兵必不能涉。

translations.literal: Eighteen li northeast of Haozhou there was a ford; Tang men fortified it and surrounded themselves with water, believing Zhou troops could certainly not cross.
translations.idiomatic: Eighteen li northeast of Haozhou lay a ford; Tang forces fortified it and ringed themselves with water, assuming Zhou troops could never cross.

sentences.zh: 戊子，帝自攻之，命內殿直康保裔帥甲士數百，乘橐駝涉水，太祖皇帝帥騎兵繼之，遂拔之。

translations.literal: On wuzi the Emperor personally attacked it, ordering Inner Palace Direct Kang Baoyi to lead several hundred armored soldiers riding camels through the water, with Zhao Kuangyin leading cavalry after them; they took it.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuzi day the Emperor attacked in person, ordering Kang Baoyi of the Inner Palace Direct to lead several hundred armored men across on camels while Zhao Kuangyin followed with cavalry; the position fell.

sentences.zh: 李重進破濠州南關城。

translations.literal: Li Chongjin broke the southern gate city of Haozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chongjin captured Haozhou's southern gate fort.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，帝自攻濠州，王審琦拔其水寨。

translations.literal: On guisi the Emperor personally attacked Haozhou; Wang Shenqi took its water camp.
translations.idiomatic: On the guisi day, Later Zhou Emperor Shizong assaulted Haozhou in person; Wang Shenqi captured its water camp.

sentences.zh: 唐人屯戰船數百於城北，又植巨木於淮水以限周兵。

translations.literal: Tang men moored several hundred warships north of the city and also planted huge logs in the Huai to block Zhou troops.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Tang forces anchored several hundred warships north of the city and drove great logs into the Huai to block Zhou movement.

sentences.zh: 帝命水軍攻之，拔其木，焚戰船七十餘艘，斬首二千餘級，又攻拔其羊馬城，城中震恐。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered the navy to attack, pulled up the logs, burned more than seventy warships, took more than two thousand heads, and also stormed and took the livestock enclosure; panic spread through the city.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent the fleet to attack, uprooted the logs, burned more than seventy warships, and killed more than two thousand men; they also took the outer livestock fort, and terror seized the city.

sentences.zh: 丙申夜，唐濠州團練使郭廷謂上表言：「臣家在江南，今若遽降，恐為唐所種族，請先遣使詣金陵稟命，然後出降。」

translations.literal: On the night of bingshen, Guo Tingwei, Tang regimental commander of Hao prefecture, submitted a memorial stating: "My family is in Jiangnan. If I surrender abruptly now, I fear Tang will exterminate my clan. I beg first to send an envoy to Jinling for orders, and then come out to surrender."
translations.idiomatic: On the night of bingshen, Guo Tingwei, Southern Tang regimental commander of Hao prefecture, memorialized, "My family remains in Jiangnan. If I surrender at once, Tang may wipe out my clan. Please let me send an envoy to Jinling for instructions before I submit."

sentences.zh: 帝許之。

translations.literal: The Emperor granted this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，帝聞唐有戰船數百艘在泗水東，欲救濠州。

translations.literal: On xinchou the Emperor heard that Tang had several hundred warships on the east of the Si River intending to relieve Haozhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinchou day the Emperor learned that several hundred Tang warships lay east of the Si River, bound to relieve Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 自將兵夜發水陸擊之。

translations.literal: He himself led troops by night, setting out by land and water to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: He led a force out by night, attacking by land and water together.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，大破唐兵於洞口，斬首五千餘級，降卒二千餘人，因鼓行而東，所至皆下。

translations.literal: On guimao he inflicted a great defeat on Tang troops at Dongkou, taking more than five thousand heads and more than two thousand surrendered soldiers; then advancing to the drumbeat eastward, everywhere he reached submitted.
translations.idiomatic: On the guimao day he routed the Tang fleet at Dongkou, killing more than five thousand and capturing more than two thousand; marching east to the beat of drums, every place he reached fell.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，至泗州城下，太祖皇帝先攻其南，因焚城門，破水寨及月城。

translations.literal: On yisi he reached beneath Si prefecture city. Zhao Kuangyin first attacked the south, then burned the city gate and broke the water camp and moon city.
translations.idiomatic: On the yisi day he reached Si prefecture. Zhao Kuangyin struck the south first, burned the gate, and broke the water camp and outer moon city.

sentences.zh: 帝居於月城樓，督將士攻城。

translations.literal: The Emperor lodged in the moon-city tower and supervised the officers and soldiers in assaulting the city.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhou Emperor Shizong took up position in the moon-city tower and directed the assault.

sentences.zh: 北漢主自即位以來，方安集境風，未遑外略。

translations.literal: Since the Northern Han ruler acceded to the throne, he had been settling conditions within his borders and had not yet turned to external campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: Since taking the throne, the Northern Han ruler had been consolidating his realm and had not yet looked outward.

sentences.zh: 是月，契丹遣其大同節度使、侍中崔勳將兵來會北漢，欲同入寇。

translations.literal: That month the Khitan sent their Datong military governor and palace attendant Cui Xun to lead troops to join Northern Han, intending to invade together.
translations.idiomatic: That month the Khitan sent Cui Xun, their Datong military governor and palace attendant, to join Northern Han for a joint invasion.

sentences.zh: 北漢主遣其忠武節度使、同平章事李存瑰將兵會之，南侵潞州，至其城下而還。

translations.literal: The Northern Han ruler sent his Zhongwu military governor and concurrent Grand Chancellor Li Cungui to lead troops to meet them, invading south to Lu prefecture, reaching beneath its walls and then returning.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Han ruler sent Li Cungui, military governor of Zhongwu and concurrent grand chancellor, to meet them; they raided south to Lu prefecture, reached its walls, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 北漢主知契丹不足恃而不敢遽與之絕，贈送勳甚厚。

translations.literal: The Northern Han ruler knew the Khitan could not be relied on yet did not dare break with them abruptly; he sent Cui Xun very generous gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the Khitan were unreliable, the Northern Han ruler still dared not break with them outright and sent Cui Xun lavish gifts.

sentences.zh: 十二月，乙卯，唐泗州守將范再遇舉城降，以再遇為宿州團練使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on yimao, Fan Zaiyu, Tang defending general of Si prefecture, surrendered the city; Zaiyu was made regimental commander of Su prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the yimao day, Fan Zaiyu, Southern Tang defender of Si prefecture, surrendered the city and was made regimental commander of Su prefecture.

sentences.zh: 上自至泗州城下，禁軍中芻蕘者毋得犯民田，民皆感悅，爭獻芻粟；

translations.literal: Since the Emperor had personally reached beneath Si prefecture city, he forbade those in the army gathering fodder from violating the people's fields; the people were all moved and pleased and competed to offer fodder and grain;
translations.idiomatic: From the time Later Zhou Emperor Shizong reached Si prefecture, he forbade foragers to trample civilian fields; the people were grateful and vied to bring fodder and grain;

sentences.zh: 既克泗州，無一卒敢擅入城者。

translations.literal: after Si prefecture was taken, not a single soldier dared enter the city without authorization.
translations.idiomatic: after Si fell, not one soldier dared enter the city unbidden.

sentences.zh: 帝聞唐戰船數百艘泊洞口，遣騎詗之，唐兵退保清口。

translations.literal: The Emperor heard that several hundred Tang warships were moored at Dongkou and sent cavalry to reconnoiter; Tang troops withdrew to defend Qingkou.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that several hundred Tang warships lay at Dongkou, the Emperor sent cavalry to scout; the Tang fleet fell back to Qingkou.

sentences.zh: 戊午旦，上自將親軍自淮北進，命太祖皇帝將步騎自淮南進，諸將以水軍自中流進，共追唐兵。

translations.literal: At dawn on wuwu the Emperor himself led the personal guard advancing from north of the Huai, ordered Zhao Kuangyin to lead infantry and cavalry advancing from south of the Huai, and the generals to lead the navy advancing from midstream, jointly pursuing Tang troops.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on the wuwu day the Emperor led his personal guard from north of the Huai, ordered Zhao Kuangyin to advance with infantry and cavalry from the south bank, and sent the fleet up the middle of the river—all closing on the Tang force.

sentences.zh: 時淮濱久無行人，葭葦如織，多泥淖溝塹，士卒乘勝氣茇涉爭進，皆忘其勞。

translations.literal: At the time the Huai banks had long been without travelers; reeds were woven like cloth and there were many muddy swamps and ditches. Soldiers, riding the momentum of victory, waded and scrambled forward, all forgetting their fatigue.
translations.idiomatic: The Huai banks had long been deserted; reeds stood thick as woven cloth and mud and ditches abounded. Drunk on victory, the troops splashed and scrambled forward, forgetting their weariness.

sentences.zh: 庚申，追及唐兵，且戰且行，金鼓聲聞數十里。

translations.literal: On gengshen they caught up with Tang troops, fighting as they marched; the sound of drums and bells was heard for several tens of li.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengshen day they overtook the Tang force, fighting as they marched; drums and gongs carried for dozens of li.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，至楚州西北，大破之。

translations.literal: On xinyou they reached northwest of Chu prefecture and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinyou day they reached northwest of Chu prefecture and won a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 唐兵有沿淮東下者，帝自追之，太祖皇帝為前鋒，行六十里，擒其保義節度使、濠、泗、楚、海都應援使陳承昭以歸。

translations.literal: Tang troops fleeing east along the Huai—the Emperor personally pursued them, with Zhao Kuangyin as vanguard. After marching sixty li they captured Chen Chengzhao, military governor of Baoyi and overall relief commissioner for Hao, Si, Chu, and Hai, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Tang troops fleeing down the Huai were pursued by the Emperor in person, with Zhao Kuangyin in the van. After sixty li they captured Chen Chengzhao, military governor of Baoyi and overall relief commissioner for Hao, Si, Chu, and Hai.

sentences.zh: 所獲戰船燒沉之餘得三百餘艘，士卒殺溺之餘得七千餘人。

translations.literal: Of warships captured, after burning and sinking, more than three hundred remained; of soldiers, after killing and drowning, more than seven thousand remained.
translations.idiomatic: Of the enemy fleet, more than three hundred hulls survived burning and sinking; of the enemy troops, more than seven thousand survived killing and drowning.

sentences.zh: 唐之戰船在淮上者，於是盡矣。

translations.literal: Tang warships on the Huai were thus entirely gone.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Tang warships on the Huai were now gone entirely.

sentences.zh: 郭廷謂使者自金陵還，知唐不能救，命錄事參軍鄱陽李延鄒草降表。

translations.literal: When Guo Tingwei's envoy returned from Jinling and knew Tang could not save him, he ordered recording officer Li Yanzhou of Poyang to draft a surrender memorial.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Tingwei's envoy returned from Jinling with word that Tang could not help him, he ordered Li Yanzhou, recording officer of Poyang, to draft a surrender memorial.

sentences.zh: 延鄒責以忠義，廷謂以兵臨之，延鄒擲筆曰：「大丈夫終不負國為叛臣作降表！」

translations.literal: Yanzhou rebuked him on grounds of loyalty and integrity. Tingwei pressed him with troops; Yanzhou threw down his brush and said: "A great man will never betray his state by writing a surrender memorial for a rebel minister!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Yanzhou rebuked him for betraying loyalty. Guo Tingwei threatened him with troops; Li Yanzhou threw down his brush and said, "No true man writes a surrender for a traitor!"

sentences.zh: 廷謂斬之，舉濠州降，得兵萬人，糧數萬斛。

translations.literal: Tingwei executed him, then surrendered Haozhou, obtaining ten thousand troops and tens of thousands of hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Tingwei had him executed, then surrendered Haozhou with ten thousand troops and tens of thousands of hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 唐主賞李延鄒之子以官。

translations.literal: The Southern Tang ruler rewarded Li Yanzhou's son with an office.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Tang ruler rewarded Li Yanzhou's son with an official post.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，帝濟淮，至楚州，營於城西北。

translations.literal: On renxu the Emperor crossed the Huai and reached Chu prefecture, encamping northwest of the city.
translations.idiomatic: On the renxu day, Later Zhou Emperor Shizong crossed the Huai to Chu prefecture and encamped northwest of the city.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，唐雄武軍使、知漣水縣事崔萬迪降。

translations.literal: On yichou Cui Wandi, Tang commissioner of the Xiongwu Army and administrator of Lianshui county, surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: On the yichou day, Cui Wandi, Southern Tang commissioner of the Xiongwu Army and magistrate of Lianshui county, surrendered.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，以郭廷謂為亳州防禦使。

translations.literal: On bingyin Guo Tingwei was made defender commissioner of Bo prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingyin day, Guo Tingwei was appointed defender commissioner of Bo prefecture.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，帝攻楚州，克其月城。

translations.literal: On wuchen the Emperor attacked Chu prefecture and took its moon city.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuchen day, the Emperor assaulted Chu prefecture and captured its moon city.

sentences.zh: 庚午，郭廷謂見於行宮，帝曰：「朕南征以來，江南諸將敗亡相繼，獨卿能斷渦口浮梁，破定遠寨，所以報國足矣。

translations.literal: On gengwu Guo Tingwei was received at the mobile palace. The Emperor said: "Since my southern campaign, Jiangnan generals have fallen one after another; you alone were able to cut the pontoon bridge at Wokou and break the camp at Dingyuan—your service to your state is enough.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengwu day, Guo Tingwei was received at the field palace. The Emperor said, "Since this southern campaign, Jiangnan generals have fallen one after another; you alone cut the Wokou pontoon bridge and broke the camp at Dingyuan—you have done enough for your country.

sentences.zh: 濠州小城，使李璟自守，能守之乎！」

translations.literal: Haozhou is a small city—if Li Jing holds it himself, can he hold it!"
translations.idiomatic: Haozhou is a small town—could Li Jing hold it even if he tried?"

sentences.zh: 使將濠州兵攻天長。

translations.literal: He then ordered him to lead Hao prefecture troops to attack Tianchang.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Guo Tingwei to lead the Hao garrison against Tianchang.

sentences.zh: 帝遣鐵騎左廂都指揮使武守琦將騎數百趨揚州，至高郵。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Wu Shouqi, commander of the Left Wing of the Iron Cavalry, to lead several hundred horsemen toward Yangzhou, reaching Gaoyou.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Wu Shouqi, commander of the Left Wing of the Iron Cavalry, with several hundred horsemen toward Yangzhou as far as Gaoyou.

sentences.zh: 唐人悉焚揚州官府民居，驅其人南渡江。

translations.literal: Tang men burned all government offices and private dwellings in Yangzhou and drove the people south across the river.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Tang forces burned Yangzhou's government offices and private homes and drove the population south across the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 後數日，周兵至，城中餘癃病十餘人而已；

translations.literal: Several days later Zhou troops arrived; in the city there remained only a dozen-odd sick and infirm;
translations.idiomatic: Days later Zhou troops arrived to find only a dozen or so sick and aged people left in the city;

sentences.zh: 癸酉，守琦以聞。

translations.literal: On guiyou Shouqi reported this.
translations.idiomatic: on the guiyou day, Wu Shouqi reported this.

sentences.zh: 帝聞泰州無備，遣兵襲之，丁丑，拔泰州。

translations.literal: The Emperor heard that Taizhou was undefended and sent troops to raid it; on dingchou Taizhou was taken.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Taizhou was undefended, the Emperor sent a raiding force; on the dingchou day Taizhou fell.

sentences.zh: 南漢中書侍郎、同平章事盧膺卒。

translations.literal: Lu Ying, Vice Director of the Secretariat and concurrent Grand Chancellor of Southern Han, died.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ying, vice director of the Secretariat and concurrent grand chancellor of Southern Han, died.

sentences.zh: 南漢主聞唐屢敗，憂形於色，遣使入貢於周，為湖南所閉，乃治戰艦，修武備。

translations.literal: When the Southern Han ruler heard that Tang had repeatedly been defeated, worry showed on his face. He sent envoys to offer tribute to Zhou, but Hunan blocked the route; he then built warships and repaired armaments.
translations.idiomatic: When the Southern Han ruler heard of Tang's repeated defeats, worry showed on his face. He sent envoys to tribute Zhou, but Hunan blocked the way; he then built warships and repaired his defenses.

sentences.zh: 既而縱酒酣飲，曰：「吾身得免，幸矣，何暇慮後世哉！」

translations.literal: Soon afterward he gave himself to heavy drinking and said: "I myself have escaped harm—that is fortune enough. What leisure is there to worry about later generations!"
translations.idiomatic: Soon he drowned his fears in wine and said, "I have saved my own skin—that is luck enough. Why worry about those who come after?"

sentences.zh: 唐使者陳處堯在契丹，白契丹主請南遊太原，北漢主厚禮之。

translations.literal: Tang envoy Chen Chuyao was in Khitan territory and asked the Khitan ruler's permission to travel south to Taiyuan; the Northern Han ruler treated him with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Tang envoy Chen Chuyao, detained in Khitan lands, asked the Khitan ruler to let him visit Taiyuan; the Northern Han ruler received him with great honor.

sentences.zh: 留數日，北還，竟卒於契丹。

translations.literal: After several days he returned north, but in the end died in Khitan territory.
translations.idiomatic: After several days he started back north but died in Khitan territory before reaching home.
